recipes.name: Berry Greek Yogurt Overnight Oats
steps: Stir the oats, Greek yogurt, milk, chia seeds, honey and cinnamon together in a big bowl.
Split into 5 jars and top each with a handful of frozen berries (they thaw overnight).
Lid and refrigerate. Eat cold, straight from the jar, within 5 days.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
tools: 5 jars or containers with lids (about 12 oz each)
prep: Measure 2.5 cups rolled oats, 2.5 cups Greek yogurt and 2.5 cups milk.
Measure 2.5 tbsp chia seeds, 2 tbsp honey and 1 tsp cinnamon.
Leave the berries in the freezer until the end.
steps: Spoon the Greek yogurt into the bowl and whisk in the milk until smooth, so there are no lumps of yogurt.
Add the honey and cinnamon and whisk again until the honey has dissolved.
Stir in the oats and chia seeds. Mix well, scraping the bottom, so every oat is wet.
Divide the mixture evenly between the 5 jars (about 1 cup each).
Top each jar with a handful of frozen berries. Don't stir them in; they thaw on top overnight and keep their colour.
Put the lids on and refrigerate at least 6 hours or overnight so the oats and chia soften.
tips: It thickens as it sits. If it's too thick in the morning, stir in a splash of milk.
Eat it cold. If you want it warm, microwave 1 minute without the lid and stir.
guide.safe: No meat or eggs to undercook: cook until the vegetables are tender and the sauce is hot all the way through.
guide.store: Keep sealed in the fridge and eat within 4 days.
guide.reheat: Best eaten cold. To warm it, microwave 60 to 90 seconds without the lid and stir.

recipes.name: Veggie Cheddar Egg Muffins
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Chop the spinach, pepper and onion small and divide them between the cups.
Whisk the eggs with garlic powder, salt and pepper, pour over the vegetables, and top with cheddar.
Bake 20 to 22 minutes until set in the middle. Cool, then refrigerate 3 per serving.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Finely chop 3 oz spinach, 1 bell pepper and half an onion.
Spray all 12 muffin cups well, including the sides.
steps: Divide the chopped spinach, pepper and onion evenly between the 12 cups, about 2 tablespoons each.
Crack the 12 eggs into the bowl. Add the garlic powder, 1/2 tsp salt and a few grinds of pepper, and whisk until no streaks of white remain.
Pour the egg over the vegetables, filling each cup about three-quarters full.
Sprinkle the shredded cheddar over the tops.
Bake 20 to 22 minutes, until the middles are set and don't jiggle, and a knife pushed into the centre comes out clean.
Let them cool in the tin 5 minutes, then run a knife round each one and lift them out.
Cool completely, then pack 3 per container.
tips: They puff in the oven and sink a little as they cool; that's normal.
Cool them fully before sealing, or steam makes them soggy.
guide.safe: Eggs are done when the whites are firm and the yolks are thickened. Baked egg dishes are safe at 160°F in the middle.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave 2 muffins for 45 to 60 seconds, until hot in the middle (165°F).

recipes.name: Black Bean Breakfast Burritos
steps: Scramble the eggs over medium-low heat until just set; season with cumin, salt and pepper.
Warm the drained black beans with the salsa for 2 minutes.
Fill each tortilla with eggs, beans and cheese, roll tightly, and wrap in foil.
Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze. Reheat 1 to 2 minutes in the microwave (foil off).

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Drain and rinse the black beans.
Crack the 10 eggs into a bowl with the cumin, 1/2 tsp salt and some pepper, and whisk.
Tear 6 sheets of foil big enough to wrap a burrito.
steps: Heat the non-stick pan on medium-low with a little oil or cooking spray.
Pour in the eggs. Wait 20 seconds, then slowly push them from the edges to the middle with the spatula, making soft curds.
Keep stirring gently for 3 to 4 minutes. Take the pan off the heat while the eggs still look slightly wet; they finish cooking from their own heat.
In the saucepan, warm the beans with the salsa on medium for 2 minutes, stirring, until hot.
Warm the tortillas 10 seconds each in the microwave so they fold without cracking.
Down the middle of each tortilla, add eggs, a spoonful of beans and a little cheddar. Don't overfill.
Fold the sides in, then roll tightly from the bottom. Wrap each one in foil.
Cool, then refrigerate or freeze.
tips: Let the bean mix cool a few minutes before filling, so the tortillas don't go soggy.
guide.safe: Eggs are done when the whites are firm and the yolks are thickened. Baked egg dishes are safe at 160°F in the middle.
guide.store: Refrigerate up to 4 days, or freeze up to 3 months.
guide.reheat: Take the foil off. Wrap in a damp paper towel and microwave 1 to 2 minutes from the fridge, or 2 to 3 minutes from frozen, turning halfway, until hot in the middle.

recipes.name: Peanut Butter Banana Baked Oatmeal
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and grease an 8x8 baking dish.
Mash the bananas, then whisk in the eggs, milk, peanut butter, honey and cinnamon.
Stir in the oats and pour into the dish.
Bake about 30 minutes until golden and set. Cut into 6 squares.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Grease the baking dish with a little oil or cooking spray.
steps: Peel the 2 bananas and mash them in the bowl with a fork until mostly smooth.
Add the 2 eggs, 2 cups milk, 4 tbsp peanut butter, 2 tbsp honey and 1 tsp cinnamon. Whisk until the peanut butter is mixed in.
Stir in the 3 cups oats and a pinch of salt.
Pour into the dish and spread it level.
Bake about 30 minutes, until the top is golden and the middle is set and doesn't jiggle.
Cool 10 minutes, then cut into 6 squares.
tips: Riper bananas (with brown spots) make it sweeter.
Warm the peanut butter for 10 seconds in the microwave if it's stiff, so it mixes in easily.
guide.safe: Eggs are done when the whites are firm and the yolks are thickened. Baked egg dishes are safe at 160°F in the middle.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave a square for 45 to 60 seconds. It's also good cold.

recipes.name: High-Protein Yogurt Parfait Jars
steps: Toast the oats in a dry pan for 3 minutes and let them cool.
Stir the honey into the Greek yogurt.
Layer yogurt, berries, oats and chia in 5 jars, with a spoon of peanut butter on top.
Refrigerate. Keep the oats on top so they stay a bit crunchy.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Measure 1 cup rolled oats.
Leave the berries frozen.
steps: Put the oats in the dry pan on medium heat. Stir often for about 3 minutes, until they smell toasty and turn light golden. Tip them onto a plate to cool.
Stir the 2.5 tbsp honey into the 4 cups Greek yogurt.
In each jar, spoon in a layer of yogurt, then berries, then more yogurt.
Sprinkle the chia seeds over the top, then the toasted oats.
Add a spoonful of peanut butter on top of each jar and put the lids on.
tips: Keep the oats on top, not between the layers, so they stay crunchy.
guide.safe: No meat or eggs to undercook: cook until the vegetables are tender and the sauce is hot all the way through.
guide.store: Keep in the fridge and eat within 4 days.
guide.reheat: Eat cold; no reheating needed. The berries thaw in the fridge overnight.

recipes.name: Chicken Burrito Bowls
steps: Cook the rice. Toss the chicken in the taco seasoning and oil.
Sear the chicken 6 to 7 minutes a side until 165°F inside; rest, then slice.
Warm the drained beans and the corn together.
Divide rice, beans and corn, chicken and salsa into 6 containers; squeeze lime over.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Start the rice first (see step 1).
Drain and rinse the 2 cans of black beans.
Pat the chicken dry and toss it with the taco seasoning and 1 tbsp oil.
steps: Cook the 1.5 cups rice: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Bring the rice and twice its volume of water (for example 1.5 cups rice + 3 cups water) and a pinch of salt to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on 5 more minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Heat the skillet on medium-high. Add the chicken and cook without moving it for 6 to 7 minutes, until well browned underneath.
Flip and cook 6 to 7 minutes more, until it reads 165°F in the thickest part.
Move the chicken to a board and rest 5 minutes so it stays juicy, then slice it.
Warm the beans and corn together in the small saucepan on medium for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until hot. Season with a pinch of salt.
Divide the rice, beans and corn, chicken and salsa between the 6 containers. Squeeze the lime over the top.
tips: If the breasts are very thick, slice them in half sideways first so they cook evenly and faster.
guide.safe: Chicken is safe at 165°F in the thickest part. No thermometer? Cut the thickest piece: the juices run clear and there is no pink.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Sheet-Pan Chicken, Sweet Potatoes & Broccoli
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Cube the sweet potatoes, toss with half the oil and spices, and roast 15 minutes.
Cut the chicken into chunks and the broccoli into florets; toss with the rest of the oil and spices.
Add both to the pan and roast 15 to 18 minutes more, until the chicken is cooked through.
Divide between 5 containers.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
tools: 1 large rimmed sheet pan (or 2 if small)
prep: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Peel and cut the sweet potatoes into 3/4-inch cubes.
Cut the chicken into 1.5-inch chunks and the broccoli into bite-size florets.
Mix the smoked paprika and garlic powder with 1 tsp salt.
steps: Toss the sweet potatoes with half the oil and half the spice mix. Spread them on the pan in one layer and roast 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, toss the chicken and broccoli with the rest of the oil and spices.
Take the pan out, push the potatoes to one side and add the chicken and broccoli in one layer.
Roast 15 to 18 minutes more, until the chicken reads 165°F, the potatoes are tender and the broccoli edges are browned.
Divide between 5 containers.
tips: Crowded pans steam instead of roast. Use two pans if the food is piled up.
guide.safe: Chicken is safe at 165°F in the thickest part. No thermometer? Cut the thickest piece: the juices run clear and there is no pink.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Honey Garlic Chicken, Rice & Green Beans
steps: Cook the rice. Mix honey, soy sauce, minced garlic, cornstarch and 1/4 cup water.
Brown the chicken thighs 5 minutes a side in a hot pan.
Pour in the sauce and simmer 5 minutes until sticky and the chicken reaches 165°F.
Steam the green beans. Pack rice, chicken with sauce, and green beans into 6 containers.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Start the rice.
Mince the 4 garlic cloves.
In a small bowl mix 3 tbsp honey, 4 tbsp soy sauce, the garlic, 1 tbsp cornstarch and 1/4 cup water.
steps: Cook the 1.5 cups rice: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Bring the rice and twice its volume of water (for example 1.5 cups rice + 3 cups water) and a pinch of salt to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on 5 more minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Pat the chicken thighs dry and season lightly with pepper (the soy sauce brings the salt).
Heat a little oil in the skillet on medium-high. Add the thighs and brown 5 minutes a side.
Stir the sauce (the cornstarch sinks) and pour it into the pan. Simmer 5 minutes, turning the chicken, until the sauce is thick and sticky and the chicken reads 165°F.
Steam the green beans 4 to 5 minutes (or microwave per the bag) until bright green and tender.
Pack rice, chicken with sauce, and green beans into 6 containers.
tips: Thighs stay juicy even if cooked a little past 165°F; they are often best around 175°F.
guide.safe: Chicken is safe at 165°F in the thickest part. No thermometer? Cut the thickest piece: the juices run clear and there is no pink.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Chicken & Veggie Stir-Fry
steps: Cook the rice. Slice the chicken thin and toss it with the cornstarch.
Stir-fry the chicken in a very hot pan for 5 minutes; take it out.
Stir-fry the broccoli, sliced peppers and carrots 4 minutes, then add garlic and ginger.
Return the chicken, add soy sauce, honey and sesame oil, toss 1 minute, and pack over rice.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Start the rice.
Slice the chicken into thin strips and toss with the cornstarch.
Cut the broccoli into small florets, slice the peppers and carrots thin.
Mince the garlic and grate the ginger.
Mix the soy sauce, honey and sesame oil in a cup.
steps: Cook the 1.5 cups rice: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Bring the rice and twice its volume of water (for example 1.5 cups rice + 3 cups water) and a pinch of salt to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on 5 more minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Heat a little oil in the wok on high until it shimmers.
Add the chicken in one layer and stir-fry about 5 minutes, until no pink remains (165°F). Move it to a plate.
Add a little more oil, then the broccoli, peppers and carrots. Stir-fry 4 minutes until crisp-tender.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir 30 seconds until they smell fragrant.
Return the chicken, pour in the sauce and toss 1 minute until everything is coated and glossy.
Pack over rice in 5 containers.
tips: Have everything chopped before you turn on the heat; stir-frying goes fast.
guide.safe: Chicken is safe at 165°F in the thickest part. No thermometer? Cut the thickest piece: the juices run clear and there is no pink.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Greek Chicken Bowls with Yogurt Sauce
steps: Cook the rice. Rub the chicken with oil, oregano, half the lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Cook the chicken 6 to 7 minutes a side until 165°F; rest and slice.
Stir the Greek yogurt with grated garlic, the rest of the lemon juice, a little grated cucumber and salt.
Pack rice, chicken, chopped cucumber, tomatoes and red onion, with the sauce on the side.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Start the rice.
Juice the lemon.
Rub the chicken with 2 tbsp oil, the oregano, half the lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Chop most of the cucumber, halve the cherry tomatoes and slice the red onion thin. Grate a small piece of cucumber for the sauce.
steps: Cook the 1.5 cups rice: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Bring the rice and twice its volume of water (for example 1.5 cups rice + 3 cups water) and a pinch of salt to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on 5 more minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Heat the skillet on medium-high. Cook the chicken 6 to 7 minutes a side until it reads 165°F.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes, then slice.
For the sauce, stir the Greek yogurt with 1 grated garlic clove (or 2 for strong garlic), the rest of the lemon juice, the grated cucumber and a pinch of salt.
Pack rice, chicken, cucumber, tomatoes and red onion in 5 containers, with the sauce in a small separate cup.
tips: Squeeze the grated cucumber in a paper towel so the sauce doesn't go watery.
guide.safe: Chicken is safe at 165°F in the thickest part. No thermometer? Cut the thickest piece: the juices run clear and there is no pink.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Reheat only the rice and chicken (take the vegetables and sauce out first), 1.5 to 2 minutes until steaming. Add the cold vegetables and sauce after.

recipes.name: Sheet-Pan Chicken Fajitas
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Slice the chicken, peppers and onion into strips.
Toss everything with oil and taco seasoning on a big sheet pan.
Roast 20 minutes, stirring once, until the chicken is cooked and the peppers char at the edges.
Squeeze lime over. Pack with 2 tortillas per serving.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Slice the chicken into strips about 1/2 inch thick.
Slice the 3 peppers and the onion into strips.
steps: Toss the chicken, peppers and onion with the 2 tbsp oil and the taco seasoning in a big bowl.
Spread everything on the sheet pan in one layer.
Roast 20 minutes, stirring once halfway, until the chicken reads 165°F and the peppers are soft and charred at the edges.
Squeeze the lime over everything.
Pack with 2 tortillas per serving (keep the tortillas in a bag, not touching the hot filling).
tips: Thin, even strips cook through at the same time as the vegetables.
guide.safe: Chicken is safe at 165°F in the thickest part. No thermometer? Cut the thickest piece: the juices run clear and there is no pink.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave the filling covered 1.5 to 2 minutes until steaming. Warm the tortillas 10 to 15 seconds wrapped in a damp paper towel.

recipes.name: Easy Chicken Tikka-Style Curry
steps: Cook the rice. Soften the chopped onion in a big pot for 5 minutes, then add garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the chicken in chunks and cook 5 minutes.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes and coconut milk and simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in the peas and the yogurt off the heat. Serve over rice.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Start the rice.
Chop the onion, mince the 4 garlic cloves, grate the ginger.
Cut the chicken thighs into bite-size chunks.
Take the yogurt out so it isn't fridge-cold when you stir it in.
steps: Cook the 1.5 cups rice: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Bring the rice and twice its volume of water (for example 1.5 cups rice + 3 cups water) and a pinch of salt to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on 5 more minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Heat a little oil in the pot on medium. Cook the onion 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, ginger and curry powder and stir 1 minute, until fragrant. Don't let it burn.
Add the chicken and a pinch of salt and cook 5 minutes, stirring, until the outsides are no longer pink.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes and coconut milk. Bring to a simmer, then cook gently 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the chicken reads 165°F and the sauce thickens.
Stir in the peas and cook 2 minutes. Take the pot off the heat, then stir in the yogurt.
Taste for salt. Serve over rice in 6 containers.
tips: Add the yogurt off the heat so it doesn't split.
guide.safe: Chicken is safe at 165°F in the thickest part. No thermometer? Cut the thickest piece: the juices run clear and there is no pink.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Lemon Pepper Chicken, Potatoes & Green Beans
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Cut the potatoes into chunks, toss with half the oil, and roast 20 minutes.
Rub the chicken with the rest of the oil, lemon zest, garlic powder and lots of black pepper.
Add the chicken and green beans to the pan and roast 18 to 20 minutes.
Squeeze the lemons over everything and divide into 5 containers.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Cut the potatoes into 1-inch chunks.
Zest both lemons, then cut them in half.
steps: Toss the potatoes with half the oil and a pinch of salt on the pan. Roast 20 minutes.
Rub the chicken with the rest of the oil, the lemon zest, garlic powder, 1 tsp salt and plenty of black pepper.
Push the potatoes aside and add the chicken and frozen green beans to the pan.
Roast 18 to 20 minutes, until the chicken reads 165°F and the potatoes are golden and tender.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes and slice it. Squeeze the lemons over everything.
Divide into 5 containers.
tips: Thick breasts? Slice them in half sideways so they're done when the potatoes are.
guide.safe: Chicken is safe at 165°F in the thickest part. No thermometer? Cut the thickest piece: the juices run clear and there is no pink.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Buffalo Chicken Stuffed Sweet Potatoes
steps: Pierce the sweet potatoes and bake at 400°F for 40 minutes (or microwave 10 to 12).
Meanwhile poach the chicken in simmering water 15 minutes, then shred it and toss with the hot sauce.
Stir the yogurt with garlic powder and a pinch of salt for a cool sauce.
Split each potato, fill with buffalo chicken, and top with sauce and green onions.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Scrub the sweet potatoes and prick them all over with a fork.
Slice the green onions.
steps: Bake the sweet potatoes on the sheet about 40 minutes, until a knife slides in easily. (Or microwave 10 to 12 minutes, turning halfway.)
Meanwhile put the chicken in the saucepan, cover with water by an inch and bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer 15 minutes, until the chicken reads 165°F in the thickest part.
Lift the chicken out, shred it with two forks, and toss it with the 4 tbsp hot sauce.
Stir the Greek yogurt with the garlic powder and a pinch of salt.
Split each potato open, fill with buffalo chicken, and top with the yogurt sauce and green onions.
tips: Pack the yogurt sauce separately if you'll reheat these.
guide.safe: Chicken is safe at 165°F in the thickest part. No thermometer? Cut the thickest piece: the juices run clear and there is no pink.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Reheat the potato and chicken 2 to 3 minutes until steaming, then add the cold sauce and green onions.

recipes.name: Chicken, Spinach & Tomato Pasta
steps: Boil the pasta; save a cup of the water before draining.
Cook bite-size chicken with Italian seasoning in the oil for 7 minutes.
Add garlic and halved tomatoes for 3 minutes, then the spinach until it wilts.
Toss in the pasta, parmesan and a splash of pasta water. Divide into 6.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces.
Halve the cherry tomatoes and slice the 4 garlic cloves.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta as the package says. Save a mug of the cooking water, then drain.
Meanwhile heat the 2 tbsp oil in the skillet on medium-high. Add the chicken, Italian seasoning and a pinch of salt.
Cook about 7 minutes, stirring, until browned and 165°F inside.
Add the garlic and tomatoes and cook 3 minutes, until the tomatoes soften.
Add the spinach a handful at a time and stir until it wilts.
Add the pasta, parmesan and a splash of the pasta water. Toss until glossy.
Divide into 6 containers.
tips: The pasta water helps the parmesan coat everything; add a little more if it looks dry.
guide.safe: Chicken is safe at 165°F in the thickest part. No thermometer? Cut the thickest piece: the juices run clear and there is no pink.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Teriyaki Chicken & Broccoli Bowls
steps: Cook the rice. Whisk soy sauce, honey, garlic, ginger, cornstarch and 1/2 cup water.
Cook the chicken in chunks 7 to 8 minutes until browned.
Pour in the sauce and simmer 2 minutes until glossy.
Steam the broccoli and pack it with rice and teriyaki chicken.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Start the rice.
Cut the chicken thighs into chunks.
Mince the garlic and grate the ginger.
Whisk 5 tbsp soy sauce, 3 tbsp honey, the garlic, ginger, 1 tbsp cornstarch and 1/2 cup water.
steps: Cook the 1.5 cups rice: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Bring the rice and twice its volume of water (for example 1.5 cups rice + 3 cups water) and a pinch of salt to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on 5 more minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Heat a little oil in the skillet on medium-high. Cook the chicken 7 to 8 minutes, turning, until browned and 165°F.
Whisk the sauce again and pour it in. Simmer 2 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy.
Steam the broccoli (or microwave per the bag) until tender.
Pack rice, broccoli and teriyaki chicken in 6 containers.
tips: If the sauce gets too thick, loosen it with a splash of water.
guide.safe: Chicken is safe at 165°F in the thickest part. No thermometer? Cut the thickest piece: the juices run clear and there is no pink.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Hearty Chicken Noodle Soup
steps: Soften the chopped onion, carrots and celery in a big pot for 6 minutes; add garlic.
Add the broth, whole chicken breasts and Italian seasoning; simmer 20 minutes.
Lift out the chicken and shred it. Add the pasta and cook 8 minutes.
Return the chicken, season with salt and pepper, and portion into 6.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Chop the onion, slice the 3 carrots and 3 celery stalks.
Mince the 3 garlic cloves.
steps: Heat a little oil in the pot on medium. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook 6 minutes until starting to soften.
Add the garlic and stir 30 seconds.
Add the 8 cups broth, the whole chicken breasts and the Italian seasoning. Bring to a boil, then lower to a gentle simmer.
Simmer 20 minutes, until the chicken reads 165°F.
Lift out the chicken and shred it with two forks.
Add the pasta to the simmering soup and cook about 8 minutes, until tender.
Return the chicken. Season with salt and pepper to taste and portion into 6.
tips: Pasta keeps soaking up broth in the fridge. Add a splash of water or broth when you reheat.
guide.safe: Chicken is safe at 165°F in the thickest part. No thermometer? Cut the thickest piece: the juices run clear and there is no pink.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: BBQ Chicken, Corn & Roasted Potatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Roast the potato chunks with oil and paprika for 20 minutes.
Add the chicken to the pan, brush it with half the BBQ sauce, and roast 18 minutes.
Warm the corn. Brush the chicken with the rest of the sauce and slice.
Divide chicken, potatoes and corn into 5 containers.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Cut the potatoes into 1-inch chunks.
steps: Toss the potatoes with the 2 tbsp oil, the smoked paprika and a pinch of salt. Roast 20 minutes.
Push the potatoes aside, add the chicken and brush it with half the BBQ sauce.
Roast 18 minutes, until the chicken reads 165°F.
Warm the corn in a saucepan or the microwave.
Brush the chicken with the rest of the BBQ sauce, rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Divide the chicken, potatoes and corn into 5 containers.
tips: BBQ sauce has sugar and burns fast; adding half at the end keeps it from charring.
guide.safe: Chicken is safe at 165°F in the thickest part. No thermometer? Cut the thickest piece: the juices run clear and there is no pink.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Turkey & Three-Bean Chili
steps: Brown the turkey with the chopped onion and pepper for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, chili powder and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the beans (drained), crushed tomatoes and 1 cup water; simmer 25 minutes.
Taste for salt. Portion into 8; it freezes well.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Chop the onion and bell pepper, mince the 3 garlic cloves.
Drain and rinse the black and kidney beans.
steps: Heat a little oil in the pot on medium-high. Add the turkey, onion and pepper and cook 8 minutes, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains (165°F).
Add the garlic, chili powder and cumin and stir 1 minute.
Add the beans, crushed tomatoes and 1 cup water. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat.
Simmer uncovered 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
Taste and add salt (usually about 1 tsp). Portion into 8.
tips: Chili tastes even better the next day.
It freezes well flat in freezer bags.
guide.safe: Ground turkey is safe at 165°F. It should be browned all the way through with no pink left.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: One-Pot Turkey Taco Rice
steps: Brown the turkey with the taco seasoning in a deep pan.
Stir in the rice, salsa and broth; bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low 18 minutes until the rice is tender.
Stir in the beans and corn, top with cheddar, and portion into 6.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
tools: Deep skillet or pot with a tight lid
prep: Drain and rinse the black beans.
Rinse the rice in a sieve.
steps: Brown the turkey with the taco seasoning in the pan on medium-high for about 7 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains (165°F).
Stir in the rice, salsa and 3 cups broth. Bring to a boil.
Cover tightly, turn the heat to low, and simmer 18 minutes without lifting the lid.
Check the rice is tender. If not, cover and cook 3 to 5 minutes more.
Stir in the beans and corn, sprinkle the cheddar on top, cover 2 minutes to melt, and portion into 6.
tips: Keep the lid on while it simmers so the rice cooks evenly.
guide.safe: Ground turkey is safe at 165°F. It should be browned all the way through with no pink left.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Turkey Meatballs & Whole Wheat Spaghetti
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Mix the turkey, egg, oats, parmesan, Italian seasoning and garlic; roll 24 meatballs.
Bake 18 minutes. Boil the pasta.
Simmer the meatballs in the marinara 5 minutes.
Toss with the pasta and divide into 6.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Mince the 2 garlic cloves.
steps: In the bowl, mix the turkey, egg, 1/2 cup oats, 4 tbsp parmesan, Italian seasoning, garlic and 1/2 tsp salt with your hands until just combined. Don't overmix or they get tough.
Roll into 24 balls (about 1.5 inches; a heaping tablespoon each) and set them on the sheet pan.
Bake 18 minutes, until browned and 165°F in the middle of a meatball.
Meanwhile boil the pasta in salted water as the package says, then drain.
Warm the marinara in the saucepan, add the meatballs and simmer gently 5 minutes.
Toss with the pasta and divide into 6 containers (4 meatballs each).
tips: Wet your hands with cold water so the mix doesn't stick while rolling.
guide.safe: Ground turkey is safe at 165°F. It should be browned all the way through with no pink left.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Beef & Broccoli Rice Bowls
steps: Cook the rice. Whisk soy sauce, honey, cornstarch and 1/3 cup water.
Brown the beef with garlic and ginger, breaking it up.
Add the broccoli florets and 2 tablespoons water; cover and steam 4 minutes.
Pour in the sauce, toss until glossy, and pack over rice.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Start the rice.
Cut the broccoli into small florets.
Mince the garlic and grate the ginger.
Whisk 4 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp cornstarch and 1/3 cup water.
steps: Cook the 1.5 cups rice: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Bring the rice and twice its volume of water (for example 1.5 cups rice + 3 cups water) and a pinch of salt to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on 5 more minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Heat the skillet on medium-high. Add the beef and cook, breaking it up, about 6 minutes until browned with no pink left (160°F). Spoon off extra fat if there is a lot.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir 1 minute.
Add the broccoli and 2 tbsp water, cover and steam 4 minutes, until bright green and just tender.
Stir the sauce again, pour it in and toss 1 to 2 minutes until glossy and thick.
Pack over rice in 6 containers.
tips: Fresh broccoli works best here; frozen releases water and thins the sauce.
guide.safe: Ground beef and pork are safe at 160°F (no pink left). Whole cuts like steak, pork chops and tenderloin are safe at 145°F, then rest 3 minutes before slicing.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Hidden-Veggie Beef Bolognese
steps: Grate the carrots and zucchini and chop the onion.
Brown the beef, then add the vegetables and garlic and cook 8 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes and Italian seasoning; simmer 20 minutes. Boil the pasta meanwhile.
Toss pasta with sauce, add parmesan, and divide into 6.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Grate the 2 carrots and the zucchini on the large holes.
Chop the onion and mince the 3 garlic cloves.
steps: Brown the beef in the deep pan on medium-high, breaking it up, about 6 minutes, until no pink is left (160°F).
Add the onion, carrot, zucchini and garlic and cook 8 minutes, stirring, until soft and most of the liquid has cooked off.
Add the crushed tomatoes, Italian seasoning and 1/2 tsp salt. Simmer gently 20 minutes, stirring now and then.
Meanwhile boil the pasta in salted water as the package says and drain.
Toss the pasta with the sauce and the 3 tbsp parmesan. Divide into 6.
tips: The grated vegetables melt into the sauce, so picky eaters won't notice them.
guide.safe: Ground beef and pork are safe at 160°F (no pink left). Whole cuts like steak, pork chops and tenderloin are safe at 145°F, then rest 3 minutes before slicing.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Turkey Shepherd's Pie
steps: Boil the peeled potato chunks 15 minutes, then mash with the milk and salt.
Brown the turkey with the onion and garlic; add the frozen vegetables, broth and tomato sauce and simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch mixed with a little water to thicken.
Spread in a baking dish, top with mash, and bake at 400°F for 20 minutes.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Peel the 3 lb potatoes and cut into 2-inch chunks.
Chop the onion and mince the garlic.
Heat the oven to 400°F.
steps: Put the potatoes in the pot, cover with cold salted water and bring to a boil. Boil about 15 minutes until a fork slides in easily.
Drain, then mash with the 1/2 cup milk and 1/2 tsp salt until smooth.
Meanwhile brown the turkey with the onion and garlic in the skillet, breaking it up, about 8 minutes, until no pink is left (165°F).
Add the frozen vegetables, 1 cup broth and the half can of tomato sauce. Simmer 5 minutes.
Mix the cornstarch with 2 tbsp cold water, stir it in and simmer 1 minute until the gravy thickens.
Spread the filling in the baking dish and spread the mash over the top. Rough up the top with a fork so it browns.
Bake 20 minutes, until bubbling at the edges and golden on top. Rest 5 minutes, then cut into 6.
tips: Start the mash at the edges and work in, so the filling doesn't push up through it.
guide.safe: Ground turkey is safe at 165°F. It should be browned all the way through with no pink left.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Pork Tenderloin with Roasted Carrots & Potatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss potato chunks and carrot sticks with 2 tablespoons oil and roast 15 minutes.
Rub the pork with mustard, honey, garlic and the rest of the oil.
Add the pork to the pan and roast 20 to 25 minutes, to 145°F inside. Rest 5 minutes and slice.
Divide into 6.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Cut the potatoes into 1-inch chunks and the 6 carrots into sticks.
Mince the 4 garlic cloves.
Trim the thin silvery skin off the pork with a small knife.
steps: Toss the potatoes and carrots with 2 tbsp oil and 1/2 tsp salt on the pan. Roast 15 minutes.
Mix the mustard, honey, garlic, the last 1 tbsp oil and 1/2 tsp salt. Rub it all over the pork.
Push the vegetables aside and put the pork in the middle of the pan.
Roast 20 to 25 minutes, until the thickest part of the pork reads 145°F.
Rest the pork 5 minutes (it stays juicy), then slice into rounds.
Divide the pork and vegetables into 6 containers with any pan juices.
tips: Tenderloin is lean and dries out fast. Start checking at 18 minutes.
guide.safe: Ground pork is safe at 160°F. Pork tenderloin and chops are safe at 145°F, then rest 3 minutes before slicing; a little pink in the middle is fine at that temperature.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Cilantro-Lime Pork Carnitas Bowls
steps: Cut the pork into 2-inch chunks and rub with cumin, oregano, garlic and salt.
Simmer covered in 1 cup water and the juice of 1 lime for 30 minutes, then shred and crisp in a hot pan.
Cook the rice and stir in chopped cilantro and the other lime's juice.
Pack rice, beans, pork and salsa into 7 containers.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
tools: Large skillet or pot with a lid
prep: Cut the pork into 2-inch chunks.
Mince the 4 garlic cloves. Juice the 2 limes into separate cups.
Chop the cilantro. Drain and rinse the black beans.
steps: Rub the pork with the cumin, oregano, garlic and 1 tsp salt.
Put it in the pan with 1 cup water and the juice of 1 lime. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook gently 30 minutes, until the pork is very tender.
Meanwhile cook the 1.75 cups rice with 3.5 cups water the same way: boil, cover, low 18 minutes, rest 5. Stir in the cilantro and the other lime's juice.
Shred the pork with two forks in the pan. Turn the heat to high and cook, without stirring for a minute at a time, until the liquid is gone and the edges crisp, about 5 minutes.
Warm the beans.
Pack rice, beans, pork and salsa into 7 containers.
tips: Real carnitas use fatty pork shoulder; this lean version stays tender because it simmers first and crisps last.
guide.safe: Ground pork is safe at 160°F. Pork tenderloin and chops are safe at 145°F, then rest 3 minutes before slicing; a little pink in the middle is fine at that temperature.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Shrimp Fried Rice
steps: Cook the rice ahead and let it cool (day-old rice fries best).
Cook the shrimp 2 minutes a side and set aside.
Scramble the eggs, push aside, then stir-fry the vegetables and garlic 3 minutes.
Add the rice, soy sauce and sesame oil; fry 4 minutes. Return the shrimp and add green onions.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
tools: Saucepan with lid (cook the rice ahead)
prep: Cook the 1.5 cups rice ahead and chill it, ideally the day before, so it fries instead of steaming.
Thaw the shrimp in a bowl of cold water for 10 minutes, then pat dry. Peel if needed.
Beat the 4 eggs. Mince the garlic and slice the green onions.
steps: Heat a little oil in the wok on high. Cook the shrimp 2 minutes a side until pink and opaque. Move them to a plate.
Add a little oil, pour in the eggs and scramble until just set. Push them to one side.
Add the frozen vegetables and garlic and stir-fry 3 minutes.
Add the cold rice, breaking up clumps. Add the soy sauce and sesame oil and fry 4 minutes, tossing, until hot and lightly toasted.
Return the shrimp, add the green onions and toss 1 minute. Divide into 5.
tips: Spread fresh rice on a tray and chill 30 minutes if you didn't cook it the day before.
guide.safe: Fish is done at 145°F, or when it turns opaque and flakes easily with a fork. Shrimp are done when they turn pink and opaque and curl into a loose C shape.
guide.store: Cool the rice fast and refrigerate within 1 hour. Eat within 3 days.
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Soy-Honey Salmon, Rice & Broccoli
steps: Cook the rice. Heat the oven to 400°F.
Mix soy sauce, honey and garlic; brush it over the salmon on a sheet pan.
Toss the broccoli with the oil around the fish and bake 12 to 15 minutes.
Pack salmon, broccoli and rice into 4 containers.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
tools: Large sheet pan lined with foil
prep: Thaw the salmon overnight in the fridge (or in sealed bags in cold water for about 30 minutes). Pat dry.
Heat the oven to 400°F.
Cut the broccoli into florets. Mince the garlic.
steps: Cook the 1 cup rice: rinse, bring to a boil with 2 cups water and a pinch of salt, cover, cook on low 18 minutes, then rest 5 minutes.
Mix the 3 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp honey and the garlic.
Put the salmon on the pan and brush the sauce over it.
Toss the broccoli with the 1 tbsp oil and a pinch of salt and spread it around the fish.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily and reads 145°F.
Pack salmon, broccoli and rice into 4 containers.
tips: Thicker fillets need the full 15 minutes; thin tail pieces may be done at 10.
guide.safe: Fish is done at 145°F, or when it turns opaque and flakes easily with a fork. Shrimp are done when they turn pink and opaque and curl into a loose C shape.
guide.store: Refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.
guide.reheat: Microwave at half power 1.5 to 2 minutes so the salmon doesn't dry out, until hot (165°F).

recipes.name: Garlic Shrimp & Spinach Pasta
steps: Boil the pasta; keep a cup of the water.
Cook the garlic in the oil 1 minute, add the shrimp and cook 2 minutes a side.
Add the spinach until wilted, then the pasta, lemon juice, parmesan and a splash of pasta water.
Toss and divide into 5.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Thaw the shrimp in cold water for 10 minutes, peel if needed and pat dry.
Slice the 5 garlic cloves thin. Juice the lemon.
steps: Boil the pasta in salted water as the package says. Save a mug of the water, then drain.
Heat the 2 tbsp olive oil in the skillet on medium. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute until fragrant, not brown.
Turn the heat to medium-high, add the shrimp in one layer and cook 2 minutes a side until pink and opaque.
Add the spinach a handful at a time until it wilts.
Add the pasta, lemon juice, parmesan and a splash of pasta water. Toss until glossy. Season with salt and pepper.
Divide into 5.
tips: Shrimp go rubbery fast; take them off as soon as they're opaque.
guide.safe: Fish is done at 145°F, or when it turns opaque and flakes easily with a fork. Shrimp are done when they turn pink and opaque and curl into a loose C shape.
guide.store: Refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Red Lentil Coconut Curry
steps: Cook the rice. Soften the onion 5 minutes, then add garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the rinsed lentils, crushed tomatoes, coconut milk and 3 cups water; simmer 20 minutes, stirring.
Stir in the spinach until wilted and season with salt.
Serve over rice; it thickens as it cools.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Start the rice.
Rinse the 2 cups red lentils in the sieve until the water runs clearer.
Chop the onion, mince the 4 garlic cloves and grate the ginger.
steps: Cook the 1.5 cups rice: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Bring the rice and twice its volume of water (for example 1.5 cups rice + 3 cups water) and a pinch of salt to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on 5 more minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Heat a little oil in the pot on medium. Cook the onion 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, ginger and curry powder and stir 1 minute.
Add the lentils, crushed tomatoes, coconut milk and 3 cups water. Bring to a boil, then simmer 20 minutes, stirring often so it doesn't stick, until the lentils have broken down.
Stir in the spinach until wilted. Add salt to taste (usually about 1 tsp).
Serve over rice in 6 containers.
tips: It thickens a lot as it cools; add a splash of water when reheating.
guide.safe: No meat or eggs to undercook: cook until the vegetables are tender and the sauce is hot all the way through.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Lentil & Sweet Potato Soup
steps: Soften the chopped onion and carrots 5 minutes; add the garlic and spices.
Add the lentils, diced sweet potatoes and broth; simmer 30 minutes until tender.
Stir in the spinach, season with salt and pepper.
Portion into 6; freezes well.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Rinse the 1.5 cups brown lentils and pick out any small stones.
Peel and dice the sweet potatoes into 1/2-inch cubes. Chop the onion and carrots. Mince the garlic.
steps: Heat a little oil in the pot on medium. Cook the onion and carrots 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin and smoked paprika and stir 1 minute.
Add the lentils, sweet potatoes and 8 cups broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered 30 minutes, until the lentils and sweet potatoes are tender.
Stir in the spinach until wilted. Season with salt and pepper.
Portion into 6.
tips: For a creamier soup, mash some of the sweet potato against the side of the pot.
guide.safe: No meat or eggs to undercook: cook until the vegetables are tender and the sauce is hot all the way through.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Black Bean & Sweet Potato Burrito Bowls
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Roast cubed sweet potatoes with oil, cumin and chili powder for 25 minutes.
Cook the rice. Warm the drained beans with the corn.
Pack rice, sweet potatoes, beans and corn, and salsa into 6 containers, with a spoon of Greek yogurt as sour cream.
Add sliced avocado and lime just before eating.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Peel and cube the 2 lb sweet potatoes (3/4 inch).
Drain and rinse the 3 cans of black beans.
steps: Toss the sweet potatoes with the 2 tbsp oil, cumin, chili powder and 1/2 tsp salt. Roast 25 minutes, turning once, until tender and browned.
Cook the 1 cup rice: rinse, bring to a boil with 2 cups water and a pinch of salt, cover, cook on low 18 minutes, then rest 5 minutes.
Warm the beans and corn together until hot.
Pack rice, sweet potatoes, beans and corn, and salsa into 6 containers, with a spoon of Greek yogurt.
Slice the avocado and squeeze lime over it only when you eat.
tips: Avocado browns once cut, so slice it fresh each day.
guide.safe: No meat or eggs to undercook: cook until the vegetables are tender and the sauce is hot all the way through.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Take out the yogurt first. Microwave covered 2 minutes until hot, then add the yogurt, avocado and lime.

recipes.name: Veggie Egg Fried Rice
steps: Cook the rice ahead and let it cool.
Scramble the eggs in a hot pan and push them aside.
Stir-fry the frozen vegetables and garlic 4 minutes.
Add the rice, soy sauce and sesame oil; fry 4 minutes and finish with green onions.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
tools: Saucepan with lid (cook the rice ahead)
prep: Cook the 2 cups rice ahead and chill it, ideally the day before.
Beat the 6 eggs. Mince the garlic and slice the green onions.
steps: Heat a little oil in the wok on high. Pour in the eggs and scramble until just set. Push them to the side.
Add the frozen vegetables and garlic and stir-fry 4 minutes.
Add the cold rice, breaking up clumps. Add the soy sauce and sesame oil.
Fry 4 minutes, tossing, until everything is hot and the rice is lightly toasted.
Stir in the green onions and divide into 5.
tips: Cold, day-old rice gives separate grains instead of a sticky mush.
guide.safe: Eggs are done when the whites are firm and the yolks are thickened. Baked egg dishes are safe at 160°F in the middle.
guide.store: Cool fast and refrigerate within 1 hour. Eat within 3 days.
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Greek Chickpea Quinoa Salad Jars
steps: Cook the quinoa in 2 cups water for 15 minutes; cool.
Whisk lemon juice, olive oil, oregano, salt and pepper in the bottom of 5 jars.
Layer chickpeas, cucumber, red onion, tomatoes, quinoa and feta.
Shake into a bowl to eat. Keeps 4 days.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Rinse the 1 cup quinoa in a sieve (this removes a bitter coating).
Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Chop the cucumber, halve the tomatoes and slice the red onion thin. Juice the lemon.
steps: Bring the quinoa and 2 cups water with a pinch of salt to a boil. Cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, until the water is gone. Rest 5 minutes, fluff, and spread out to cool.
Whisk the lemon juice, 3 tbsp olive oil, oregano, 1/2 tsp salt and pepper. Divide it between the bottoms of the 5 jars.
Layer in order: chickpeas, cucumber, red onion, tomatoes, cooled quinoa, then feta on top.
Seal and refrigerate.
tips: Keeping the dressing at the bottom and the quinoa high stops everything from going soggy.
guide.safe: Only the quinoa is cooked. Cool it before packing and keep the jars cold.
guide.store: Keep sealed in the fridge and eat within 4 days.
guide.reheat: Eat cold: shake the jar into a bowl and toss.

recipes.name: White Bean & Kale Soup
steps: Soften the onion and carrots 6 minutes; add garlic and Italian seasoning.
Add the beans, tomatoes and broth; simmer 15 minutes. Mash a few beans to thicken.
Add the chopped kale for 5 minutes.
Serve with parmesan on top.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Chop the onion and 2 carrots. Mince the 4 garlic cloves.
Drain and rinse the 4 cans of white beans.
Strip the kale leaves off the stems and chop them.
steps: Heat a little oil in the pot on medium. Cook the onion and carrots 6 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and Italian seasoning and stir 1 minute.
Add the beans, diced tomatoes with juice and 6 cups broth. Simmer 15 minutes.
Mash some of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken the soup.
Add the kale and simmer 5 minutes until tender. Season with salt and pepper.
Portion into 5 and top with the parmesan when serving.
tips: Kale stems are tough; save them for a stock or discard them.
guide.safe: No meat or eggs to undercook: cook until the vegetables are tender and the sauce is hot all the way through.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Lentil Sloppy Joes
steps: Simmer the lentils in 3 cups water 20 minutes until tender; drain.
Soften the onion and pepper 5 minutes with the garlic.
Add the lentils, tomato sauce, honey, mustard and chili powder; simmer 10 minutes until thick.
Pack with buns on the side.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Rinse the 1.5 cups brown lentils.
Chop the onion and bell pepper. Mince the 2 garlic cloves.
steps: Simmer the lentils in 3 cups water about 20 minutes until tender but not mushy. Drain.
Heat a little oil in the skillet on medium. Cook the onion, pepper and garlic 5 minutes until soft.
Add the lentils, tomato sauce, honey, mustard, chili powder and 1/2 tsp salt.
Simmer 10 minutes, stirring, until thick enough to pile on a bun.
Pack the filling with the buns on the side.
tips: Toast the buns just before eating so they don't go soggy.
guide.safe: No meat or eggs to undercook: cook until the vegetables are tender and the sauce is hot all the way through.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave the filling covered 1.5 to 2 minutes until steaming, then spoon onto a bun.

recipes.name: Pasta e Fagioli
steps: Soften the onion, carrots and celery 6 minutes; add garlic.
Add the beans, tomatoes and broth; simmer 10 minutes.
Add the pasta and cook 9 minutes, then the spinach.
Top with parmesan; add a splash of water when reheating.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Chop the onion, 2 carrots and 2 celery stalks. Mince the 3 garlic cloves.
Drain and rinse the white beans.
steps: Heat a little oil in the pot on medium. Cook the onion, carrots and celery 6 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and stir 30 seconds.
Add the beans, diced tomatoes with juice and 6 cups broth. Simmer 10 minutes.
Add the pasta and simmer about 9 minutes, stirring now and then, until tender.
Stir in the spinach until wilted. Season with salt and pepper.
Portion into 6 and top with the parmesan.
tips: The pasta soaks up the broth overnight; add a splash of water when reheating.
guide.safe: No meat or eggs to undercook: cook until the vegetables are tender and the sauce is hot all the way through.

guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Cottage Cheese & Spinach Baked Ziti
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Boil the pasta 2 minutes short of done.
Stir the cottage cheese with the egg, chopped spinach and Italian seasoning.
Layer pasta, marinara, the cottage cheese mix and mozzarella in a 9x13 dish.
Bake 25 minutes until bubbling. Cut into 8.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Chop the 5 oz spinach.
steps: Boil the pasta in salted water 2 minutes less than the package says (it finishes in the oven). Drain.
Stir the 3 cups cottage cheese with the egg, spinach and Italian seasoning.
Spread a thin layer of marinara in the dish. Add half the pasta, half the remaining marinara, all the cottage cheese mix and half the mozzarella.
Add the rest of the pasta, the rest of the marinara and the rest of the mozzarella.
Bake 25 minutes, until bubbling at the edges and the middle reads 160°F. (Cover with foil for the first 15 minutes if the top browns too fast.)
Rest 10 minutes so it holds together, then cut into 8.
tips: Resting before cutting stops the squares falling apart.
guide.safe: Eggs are done when the whites are firm and the yolks are thickened. Baked egg dishes are safe at 160°F in the middle.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Herby Lemon Chicken Quinoa Bowls
steps: Cook the quinoa. Season the chicken with Italian seasoning and 1 tablespoon oil.
Cook the chicken 6 to 7 minutes a side; rest and slice.
Whisk the rest of the oil with lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Pack spinach, quinoa, chicken, tomatoes, cucumber and feta; dress when eating.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Rinse the 1 cup quinoa.
Halve the cherry tomatoes and chop the cucumber. Juice the lemon.
Rub the chicken with the Italian seasoning, 1 tbsp oil and 1/2 tsp salt.
steps: Bring the quinoa and 2 cups water with a pinch of salt to a boil, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes. Rest 5 minutes and fluff.
Heat the skillet on medium-high. Cook the chicken 6 to 7 minutes a side until it reads 165°F.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes and slice.
Shake the remaining 2 tbsp oil with the lemon juice, salt and pepper in the jar.
Pack spinach, quinoa, chicken, tomatoes, cucumber and feta in 5 containers, with the dressing on the side.
tips: Dress it only when you eat it, so the spinach stays crisp.
guide.safe: Chicken is safe at 165°F in the thickest part. No thermometer? Cut the thickest piece: the juices run clear and there is no pink.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Good cold. To warm the chicken and quinoa, take out the spinach and vegetables first and microwave 1.5 minutes.

recipes.name: Black Bean & Quinoa Chili (Vegan)
steps: Soften the onion and pepper in a big pot 6 minutes; add the garlic, chili powder and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the rinsed quinoa, crushed tomatoes, drained beans and vegetable broth.
Simmer 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the quinoa is tender and the chili is thick.
Stir in the corn for 3 minutes and season with salt. Portion into 6; it freezes well.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Chop the onion and bell pepper, mince the 3 garlic cloves.
Rinse the 3/4 cup quinoa. Drain and rinse the 3 cans of black beans.
steps: Heat a little oil in the pot on medium. Cook the onion and pepper 6 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, chili powder and cumin and stir 1 minute.
Add the quinoa, crushed tomatoes, beans and 3 cups broth. Bring to a boil.
Simmer uncovered 25 minutes, stirring now and then so it doesn't stick, until the quinoa is tender (it shows a little white ring) and the chili is thick.
Stir in the corn for 3 minutes. Season with salt (usually about 1 tsp).
Portion into 6.
tips: Add a splash of water if it gets too thick before the quinoa is done.
guide.safe: No meat or eggs to undercook: cook until the vegetables are tender and the sauce is hot all the way through.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Chickpea & Black Bean Burrito Bowls (Vegan)
steps: Cook the rice and stir in chopped cilantro and the juice of one lime.
Pan-fry the drained chickpeas in the oil with the cumin and chili powder 6 minutes until crisp at the edges.
Warm the black beans with the corn.
Pack rice, chickpeas, beans and corn, and salsa; add sliced avocado and lime when you eat.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Drain, rinse and pat dry the chickpeas (dry chickpeas crisp better).
Drain and rinse the black beans.
Chop the cilantro. Juice one lime; cut the other into wedges.
steps: Cook the 1.25 cups rice with 2.5 cups water: boil, cover, low 18 minutes, rest 5. Stir in the cilantro and the lime juice.
Heat the 1 tbsp oil in the skillet on medium-high. Add the chickpeas, cumin, chili powder and a pinch of salt and fry 6 minutes, shaking the pan, until crisp at the edges.
Warm the black beans and corn together.
Pack rice, chickpeas, beans and corn, and salsa into 5 containers.
Slice the avocado and add it with a lime wedge only when you eat.
tips: Avocado browns once cut, so slice it fresh each day.
guide.safe: No meat or eggs to undercook: cook until the vegetables are tender and the sauce is hot all the way through.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Coconut Chickpea & Sweet Potato Stew (Vegan)
steps: Cook the rice. Soften the onion 5 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the diced sweet potatoes, chickpeas, tomatoes, coconut milk and vegetable broth.
Simmer 20 minutes until the sweet potato is soft.
Stir in the spinach until wilted and serve over rice.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Peel and dice the sweet potatoes (3/4 inch).
Chop the onion, mince the 4 garlic cloves, grate the ginger.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas.
steps: Cook the 1.25 cups rice with 2.5 cups water: boil, cover, low 18 minutes, rest 5.
Heat a little oil in the pot on medium. Cook the onion 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, ginger and curry powder and stir 1 minute.
Add the sweet potatoes, chickpeas, diced tomatoes, coconut milk and 2 cups broth. Bring to a simmer.
Simmer 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sweet potato is soft.
Stir in the spinach until wilted, add salt to taste, and serve over rice in 6 containers.
tips: Mash a few pieces of sweet potato into the sauce to make it thicker.
guide.safe: No meat or eggs to undercook: cook until the vegetables are tender and the sauce is hot all the way through.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Lentil & Mushroom Bolognese (Vegan)
steps: Finely chop the mushrooms, carrots and onion and soften them in the oil 8 minutes; add the garlic.
Add the lentils, crushed tomatoes, Italian seasoning and 2 cups water; simmer 30 minutes until the lentils are tender.
Boil the pasta meanwhile.
Toss together and divide into 6.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Rinse the 1.25 cups brown lentils.
Finely chop the mushrooms, 2 carrots and the onion (small pieces make it feel 'meaty'). Mince the 4 garlic cloves.
steps: Heat the 1 tbsp oil in the deep pan on medium. Cook the mushrooms, carrots and onion 8 minutes until soft and the mushroom liquid has cooked off.
Add the garlic and stir 1 minute.
Add the lentils, crushed tomatoes, Italian seasoning, 2 cups water and 1/2 tsp salt. Simmer partly covered 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils are tender. Add water if it gets dry.
Meanwhile boil the pasta as the package says and drain.
Toss together and divide into 6.
tips: Taste a lentil before you stop: it should be soft all the way through.
guide.safe: No meat or eggs to undercook: cook until the vegetables are tender and the sauce is hot all the way through.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Kung Pao Chicken
steps: Cook the rice. Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and toss with 1 tablespoon cornstarch and 1 tablespoon soy sauce.
Whisk the rest of the soy sauce with the honey, rice vinegar, chili garlic sauce, the other tablespoon of cornstarch and 1/4 cup water.
Sear the chicken in a very hot oiled pan 5 to 6 minutes until browned; add the diced peppers, garlic and ginger for 2 minutes.
Pour in the sauce and stir until it thickens and coats everything, about 1 minute.
Stir in the peanuts and green onions and pack over rice.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Start the rice.
Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces; toss with 1 tbsp cornstarch and 1 tbsp soy sauce.
Whisk the other 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp honey, 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 2 tsp chili garlic sauce, 1 tbsp cornstarch and 1/4 cup water.
Dice the 2 peppers, mince the garlic, grate the ginger, slice the green onions.
steps: Cook the 1.5 cups rice: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Bring the rice and twice its volume of water (for example 1.5 cups rice + 3 cups water) and a pinch of salt to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on 5 more minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in the wok on high. Add the chicken in one layer and sear 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until browned and 165°F.
Add the peppers, garlic and ginger and stir-fry 2 minutes.
Stir the sauce, pour it in, and stir about 1 minute until it thickens and coats everything.
Stir in the peanuts and green onions.
Pack over rice in 5 containers.
tips: Add more chili garlic sauce for more heat.
guide.safe: Chicken is safe at 165°F in the thickest part. No thermometer? Cut the thickest piece: the juices run clear and there is no pink.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Lighter Orange Chicken & Broccoli
steps: Cook the rice. Zest one orange, then juice both (about 2/3 cup).
Toss bite-size chicken with 2 tablespoons cornstarch and a pinch of salt; pan-fry in a little oil 6 to 7 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Whisk the orange juice and zest, honey, soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, ginger and the last tablespoon of cornstarch; pour over the chicken and simmer 2 minutes until glossy.
Steam the broccoli and pack with the rice and orange chicken.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Start the rice.
Zest one orange, then juice both (about 2/3 cup).
Mince the garlic and grate the ginger.
Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces.
steps: Cook the 1.5 cups rice: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Bring the rice and twice its volume of water (for example 1.5 cups rice + 3 cups water) and a pinch of salt to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on 5 more minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Toss the chicken with 2 tbsp cornstarch and a pinch of salt.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in the skillet on medium-high. Fry the chicken 6 to 7 minutes, turning, until golden and 165°F.
Whisk the orange juice and zest, 3 tbsp honey, 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, garlic, ginger and 1 tbsp cornstarch.
Pour the sauce over the chicken and simmer 2 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy.
Steam the broccoli and pack it with the rice and orange chicken in 6 containers.
tips: Fry in two batches if the pan is crowded, so the chicken browns instead of steaming.
guide.safe: Chicken is safe at 165°F in the thickest part. No thermometer? Cut the thickest piece: the juices run clear and there is no pink.

guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Chicken Lo Mein
steps: Boil the spaghetti until just tender; drain and toss with 1 teaspoon sesame oil.
Stir-fry thin strips of chicken in a hot oiled pan 5 minutes; add the garlic.
Add shredded cabbage, matchstick carrots and sliced pepper; stir-fry 3 minutes so they stay crisp.
Add the noodles, soy sauce, hoisin and the rest of the sesame oil; toss 2 minutes and finish with green onions.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Slice the chicken into thin strips.
Shred the cabbage, cut the 2 carrots into matchsticks, slice the pepper. Mince the garlic, slice the green onions.
steps: Boil the spaghetti until just tender. Drain and toss with 1 tsp sesame oil so it doesn't stick.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in the wok on high. Stir-fry the chicken 5 minutes until 165°F. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the cabbage, carrots and pepper and stir-fry 3 minutes so they stay crisp.
Add the noodles, 5 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp hoisin and the last 1 tsp sesame oil. Toss 2 minutes until coated and hot.
Finish with the green onions and divide into 5.
tips: Use tongs to toss the noodles so they mix evenly.
guide.safe: Chicken is safe at 165°F in the thickest part. No thermometer? Cut the thickest piece: the juices run clear and there is no pink.

guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Mapo-Style Tofu with Pork
steps: Cook the rice. Cut the tofu into 1-inch cubes.
Brown the pork in a deep pan, breaking it up, 5 minutes. Add garlic, ginger and chili garlic sauce for 1 minute.
Add the broth and soy sauce, then slide in the tofu and simmer gently 5 minutes (stir carefully so it doesn't break).
Stir in the cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons water until the sauce thickens. Top with green onions; serve over rice.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Start the rice.
Cut the 2 tofu blocks into 1-inch cubes.
Mince the garlic, grate the ginger, slice the green onions. Mix the 1 tbsp cornstarch with 2 tbsp water.
steps: Cook the 1.5 cups rice: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Bring the rice and twice its volume of water (for example 1.5 cups rice + 3 cups water) and a pinch of salt to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on 5 more minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Brown the pork in the deep pan on medium-high, breaking it up, about 5 minutes until no pink is left (160°F).
Add the garlic, ginger and chili garlic sauce and stir 1 minute.
Add the 1 cup broth and 3 tbsp soy sauce. Slide in the tofu and simmer gently 5 minutes. Move the pan or push gently with a spoon instead of stirring, so the tofu doesn't break.
Stir the cornstarch mix and pour it in. Simmer about 1 minute until the sauce thickens.
Top with green onions and serve over rice in 5 containers.
tips: Traditional mapo tofu uses Sichuan peppercorns; add a pinch of ground ones if you have them.
guide.safe: Ground beef and pork are safe at 160°F (no pink left). Whole cuts like steak, pork chops and tenderloin are safe at 145°F, then rest 3 minutes before slicing.

guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Chinese Tomato & Egg Stir-Fry
steps: Cook the rice. Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt; cut the tomatoes into wedges.
Scramble the eggs in the oil over medium heat until just set, then slide them onto a plate.
Cook the tomatoes 3 to 4 minutes until juicy; add the honey, soy sauce and the cornstarch mixed with 1/4 cup water.
When the sauce thickens, fold the eggs back in with the green onions. Serve over rice.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Start the rice.
Beat the 10 eggs with a pinch of salt.
Cut the 5 tomatoes into wedges. Slice the green onions.
Mix the 1 tbsp cornstarch with 1/4 cup water.
steps: Cook the 1.5 cups rice: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Bring the rice and twice its volume of water (for example 1.5 cups rice + 3 cups water) and a pinch of salt to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on 5 more minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Heat the 1 tbsp oil in the skillet on medium. Pour in the eggs and stir slowly until soft curds form and they're just set. Slide them onto a plate.
Add the tomatoes to the pan and cook 3 to 4 minutes, until they soften and release their juice.
Add the honey, soy sauce and the cornstarch mix. Stir until the sauce thickens, about 1 minute.
Fold the eggs back in with the green onions. Serve over rice in 4 containers.
tips: Take the eggs off while they still look a little soft; they cook more when you fold them back in.
guide.safe: Eggs are done when the whites are firm and the yolks are thickened. Baked egg dishes are safe at 160°F in the middle.
