guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Cashew Chicken
steps: Cook the rice. Toss bite-size chicken with the cornstarch.
Sear the chicken in a hot oiled pan 5 minutes; take it out.
Stir-fry the onion, pepper and broccoli with the garlic 4 minutes.
Return the chicken, add soy sauce, hoisin and 3 tablespoons water, toss until glossy, then stir in the cashews. Pack over rice.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Start the rice.
Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and toss with the 1 tbsp cornstarch.
Chop the onion and pepper, cut the broccoli into small florets, mince the garlic.
steps: Cook the 1.5 cups rice: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Bring the rice and twice its volume of water (for example 1.5 cups rice + 3 cups water) and a pinch of salt to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on 5 more minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in the wok on high. Sear the chicken 5 minutes, turning, until 165°F. Move it to a plate.
Add a little oil and stir-fry the onion, pepper, broccoli and garlic 4 minutes until crisp-tender.
Return the chicken. Add 4 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp hoisin and 3 tbsp water and toss until glossy.
Stir in the cashews and pack over rice in 5 containers.
tips: Toast the cashews in a dry pan for 2 minutes first for more flavour.

recipes.name: Pork & Cabbage Dumpling Bowls
steps: Cook the rice. Brown the pork in a large pan 6 minutes; spoon off any extra fat.
Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then the shredded cabbage and grated carrots; stir-fry 5 minutes.
Season with soy sauce, rice vinegar and sesame oil (it tastes like dumpling filling).
Top with green onions and pack over rice.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Start the rice.
Shred the half cabbage thin and grate the 2 carrots.
Mince the garlic, grate the ginger, slice the green onions.
steps: Cook the 1.5 cups rice: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Bring the rice and twice its volume of water (for example 1.5 cups rice + 3 cups water) and a pinch of salt to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on 5 more minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Brown the pork in the pan on medium-high, breaking it up, about 6 minutes until no pink is left (160°F). Spoon off extra fat.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir 1 minute.
Add the cabbage and carrots and stir-fry 5 minutes until the cabbage softens.
Season with 4 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp rice vinegar and 2 tsp sesame oil.
Top with green onions and pack over rice in 6 containers.
tips: Tastes like dumpling filling. A drizzle of chili oil is great on top.

recipes.name: Sweet & Sour Pork with Pineapple
steps: Cook the rice. Cut the pork into bite-size pieces and toss with 1 tablespoon cornstarch.
Brown the pork in a hot oiled pan 6 minutes; add chunks of pepper and onion for 3 minutes.
Whisk the juice from the pineapple can with the vinegar, honey, soy sauce, tomato paste and the other tablespoon of cornstarch.
Add the pineapple chunks and the sauce; simmer 2 minutes until thick and glossy. Serve over rice.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Start the rice.
Trim the pork and cut into bite-size pieces; toss with 1 tbsp cornstarch and a pinch of salt.
Cut the 2 peppers and the onion into chunks.
Drain the pineapple, saving the juice.
steps: Cook the 1.5 cups rice: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Bring the rice and twice its volume of water (for example 1.5 cups rice + 3 cups water) and a pinch of salt to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on 5 more minutes, then fluff with a fork.

Add the peppers and onion and cook 3 minutes.
Whisk the pineapple juice with the 3 tbsp rice vinegar, 2 tbsp honey, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp tomato paste and the other 1 tbsp cornstarch.
Add the pineapple chunks and the sauce. Simmer 2 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy.
Serve over rice in 6 containers.
tips: Small, even pieces of pork cook through before the vegetables go soft.

recipes.name: Peanut Noodles with Chicken & Veggies
steps: Boil the spaghetti and rinse it in cold water. Poach the chicken 15 minutes in simmering water, then shred it.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, honey, vinegar, sriracha and 1/4 cup hot water until smooth.
Toss the noodles with the sauce, chicken, shredded cabbage, grated carrots and sliced cucumber.
Top with green onions. Good cold or warm.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Shred the cabbage, grate the 3 carrots, slice the cucumber, slice the green onions.
steps: Put the chicken in the saucepan, cover with water by an inch and bring to a gentle simmer. Simmer about 15 minutes until it reads 165°F. Shred with two forks.
Boil the spaghetti as the package says. Drain and rinse in cold water.
Whisk the 5 tbsp peanut butter, 4 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp honey, 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 2 tsp sriracha and 1/4 cup hot water until smooth.
Toss the noodles with the sauce, chicken, cabbage, carrots and cucumber.
Top with green onions and divide into 6.
tips: The sauce thickens in the fridge; stir in a spoon of warm water before eating.

recipes.name: Chicken Tortilla Soup
steps: Soften the onion and jalapeño in a big pot 5 minutes; add the garlic, cumin and chili powder.
Add the broth, tomatoes and whole chicken breasts; simmer 20 minutes, then shred the chicken in the pot.
Add the beans and corn and simmer 5 more minutes; squeeze in the lime.
Cut the tortillas into strips and bake at 400°F for 8 minutes until crisp. Pack them separately to sprinkle on top.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Chop the onion. Seed and mince the jalapeño (wear gloves or wash your hands after). Mince the 3 garlic cloves.
Drain and rinse the black beans.
Cut the 6 corn tortillas into thin strips.
steps: Heat a little oil in the pot on medium. Cook the onion and jalapeño 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin and chili powder and stir 1 minute.
Add the 6 cups broth, diced tomatoes and whole chicken breasts. Simmer 20 minutes, until the chicken reads 165°F.
Shred the chicken right in the pot with two forks.
Add the beans and corn and simmer 5 more minutes. Squeeze in the lime and season with salt.
Meanwhile spread the tortilla strips on the sheet pan with a light spray of oil and bake at 400°F about 8 minutes, until crisp.
Portion the soup into 6 and pack the strips separately.
tips: Keep the jalapeño seeds in for more heat.

recipes.name: Chicken Tinga Tacos
steps: Simmer the chicken thighs in salted water 20 minutes, then shred.
Cook the sliced onion 5 minutes. Blend the tomatoes, chipotle, garlic and oregano and pour it in.
Simmer the sauce 5 minutes, then stir in the chicken until it's coated and saucy.
Warm the tortillas and pack with the tinga, shredded cabbage and lime wedges.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Slice the onion. Shred the cabbage. Cut the limes into wedges.
Peel the 3 garlic cloves.
steps: Put the chicken thighs in the saucepan, cover with salted water and simmer 20 minutes, until they read 165°F. Shred with two forks.
Blend the diced tomatoes, 2 tbsp chipotle in adobo, garlic and oregano until smooth.
Heat a little oil in the skillet on medium. Cook the onion 5 minutes until soft.
Pour in the sauce and simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in the chicken until it's coated and saucy. Taste for salt.
Warm the tortillas and pack with the tinga, cabbage and lime wedges (about 3 tacos a serving).
tips: Chipotles are smoky and hot; use 1 tbsp for milder tinga.

recipes.name: Black Bean & Spinach Enchiladas
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Mash half the beans with the cumin, then mix in the rest with the corn and chopped spinach.
Spread a little enchilada sauce in a baking dish. Fill and roll the tortillas and lay them seam-side down.
Pour the rest of the sauce over and top with the cheddar.
Bake 20 minutes until bubbling. 2 enchiladas per serving.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Drain and rinse the black beans. Chop the spinach.
steps: Mash half the beans with the cumin. Mix in the rest of the beans, the corn and the spinach.
Spread about 1/2 cup enchilada sauce over the bottom of the dish.
Spoon filling down each tortilla, roll up and lay them seam-side down in the dish.
Pour the rest of the sauce over and sprinkle with the cheddar.
Bake 20 minutes, until bubbling and the cheese has melted.

recipes.name: Beef Burrito Bowls
steps: Cook the rice and stir in chopped cilantro and the lime juice.
Brown the beef with the taco seasoning and 1/3 cup water until saucy, about 8 minutes.
Warm the beans and corn together.
Pack rice, beef, beans and corn, and salsa into 6 containers.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.

Chop the cilantro. Juice the lime.
Drain and rinse the black beans.
steps: Cook the 1.5 cups rice: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Add the taco seasoning and 1/3 cup water and simmer 2 minutes until saucy.
Warm the beans and corn together.
Pack rice, beef, beans and corn, and salsa into 6 containers.
tips: Add a spoon of Greek yogurt as sour cream when you eat.

recipes.name: Shrimp Tacos with Lime Slaw
steps: Toss the shrimp with the oil, chili powder, cumin and salt.
Mix the shredded cabbage with the Greek yogurt, the juice of one lime and a pinch of salt.
Cook the shrimp in a hot pan 2 minutes a side until pink.
Warm the tortillas and fill with shrimp, slaw and sliced avocado. Pack the slaw separately so the tortillas stay dry.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Thaw the shrimp in cold water for 10 minutes, peel if needed and pat very dry.
Shred the cabbage. Juice one lime and cut the other into wedges.
steps: Toss the shrimp with the 1 tbsp oil, chili powder, cumin and 1/2 tsp salt.
For the slaw, mix the cabbage with the Greek yogurt, the lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Heat the skillet on medium-high. Cook the shrimp in one layer 2 minutes a side until pink and opaque.
Warm the tortillas.
Fill with shrimp, slaw and sliced avocado. For meal prep, pack the slaw and avocado separately so the tortillas stay dry.
tips: Dry shrimp sear; wet shrimp steam. Pat them well.

recipes.name: Beef & Bean Burrito Bake
steps: Cook the rice. Heat the oven to 375°F.
Brown the beef with the taco seasoning; stir in the beans, salsa and half the enchilada sauce.
Layer torn tortillas, rice and the beef mixture in a baking dish; pour the rest of the sauce on top and add the cheddar.
Bake 20 minutes. Cut into 6.

prep: Start the rice.
Heat the oven to 375°F.
Drain and rinse the black beans. Tear the 4 tortillas into pieces.
steps: Cook the 1 cup rice: rinse, bring to a boil with 2 cups water and a pinch of salt, cover, cook on low 18 minutes, then rest 5 minutes.
Brown the beef with the taco seasoning in the skillet, breaking it up, about 6 minutes until no pink is left (160°F).
Stir in the beans, the 1/2 cup salsa and half the enchilada sauce.
In the dish, layer half the tortilla pieces, all the rice, half the beef mix, the rest of the tortillas and the rest of the beef.
Pour the rest of the sauce on top and sprinkle with the cheddar.
Bake 20 minutes until bubbling. Rest 5 minutes and cut into 6.
tips: It slices more neatly after cooling a little.

recipes.name: Steak Fajita Bowls
steps: Cook the rice. Rub the steak with half the taco seasoning and 1 tablespoon oil.
Sear the steak in a very hot pan 4 minutes a side for medium; rest 5 minutes, then slice thin across the grain.
Cook the sliced peppers and onion with the rest of the seasoning and oil 6 minutes until charred at the edges.
Pack rice, peppers and steak, and squeeze lime over.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Start the rice.
Take the steak out of the fridge 20 minutes before cooking. Pat it dry.
Rub the steak with half the taco seasoning and 1 tbsp oil.
Slice the 3 peppers and the onion into strips. Cut the limes into wedges.
steps: Cook the 1.25 cups rice with 2.5 cups water: boil, cover, low 18 minutes, rest 5.
Heat the skillet on high until very hot. Sear the steak 4 minutes a side, until it reads 145°F in the middle (medium). Thicker steaks need a minute or two more.
Rest the steak on a board 5 minutes. Then slice it thin across the grain (cut across the lines in the meat, not along them).
Turn the heat to medium-high. Add the last 1 tbsp oil, the peppers, onion and the rest of the taco seasoning. Cook 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and charred at the edges.
Pack rice, peppers and steak in 5 containers and squeeze lime over.
tips: Slicing across the grain is what makes steak tender to chew.

steps: Cook the rice. Brown the beef 6 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then the soy sauce, honey and sesame oil; simmer 2 minutes until sticky.
Slice the cucumber and grate the carrots.
Pack rice, beef and the crunchy vegetables; top with green onions.

Mince the garlic and grate the ginger.
Slice the cucumber, grate the 2 carrots, slice the green onions.

recipes.name: Hearty Beef & Vegetable Stew
steps: Pat the beef dry, season with salt and pepper, and brown it in batches in the oil in a heavy pot.
Add the onion and celery for 5 minutes, then the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the broth and Italian seasoning; cover and simmer gently 1 hour.
Add chunks of potato and carrot and simmer 30 more minutes, then thicken with the cornstarch mixed in a little water.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
tools: Large heavy pot with a lid (Dutch oven)
prep: Pat the 2 lb beef dry with paper towels and season with 1 tsp salt and pepper.
Chop the onion and slice the 3 celery stalks.
Peel and cut the potatoes into 1.5-inch chunks and the 4 carrots into thick pieces (keep them for later).
steps: Heat the 1 tbsp oil in the pot on medium-high. Brown the beef in 2 or 3 batches, about 4 minutes a batch, turning until browned on several sides. Don't crowd it. Move each batch to a plate.
Turn the heat to medium. Add the onion and celery and cook 5 minutes, scraping up the brown bits.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook 1 minute.
Return the beef and its juices. Add the 4 cups broth and Italian seasoning. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook on low 1 hour. It should barely bubble.
Add the potatoes and carrots and simmer covered 30 minutes more, until the beef and vegetables are tender.
Mix the 2 tbsp cornstarch with 3 tbsp cold water, stir it in, and simmer 2 minutes until thickened. Taste for salt and portion into 6.
tips: A hard boil makes stew meat tough; keep it to a gentle simmer.
guide.safe: Stew beef is tough until it simmers long enough: it's done when a piece falls apart easily with a fork, well past the 145°F safe temperature.

recipes.name: Beef & Bean Chili
steps: Brown the beef with the onion and pepper 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, chili powder and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the drained beans, crushed tomatoes and 1 cup water; simmer 25 minutes.
Season with salt. Portion into 8; it freezes well.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Chop the onion and bell pepper, mince the 3 garlic cloves.
Drain and rinse the kidney and black beans.
steps: Brown the beef with the onion and pepper in the pot on medium-high, breaking it up, about 8 minutes until no pink is left (160°F). Spoon off extra fat.

Add the beans, crushed tomatoes and 1 cup water. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat.
Simmer uncovered 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
Season with salt (usually about 1 tsp) and portion into 8.
tips: It freezes well flat in freezer bags.

recipes.name: Lean Meatloaf, Mashed Potatoes & Green Beans
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Mix the beef, oats, egg, grated onion, half the tomato sauce and the Italian seasoning; shape a loaf on a lined pan.
Spread the rest of the tomato sauce on top and bake 50 to 55 minutes, to 160°F inside.
Meanwhile boil the potato chunks 15 minutes and mash with the milk and salt.
Steam the green beans. Slice the meatloaf into 6 and pack with mash and beans.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
tools: Rimmed sheet pan lined with foil
prep: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Grate the onion on the large holes.
Peel and chunk the 2 lb potatoes.
steps: In the bowl, mix the beef, 1/2 cup oats, egg, grated onion, half of the half-can of tomato sauce, Italian seasoning and 1 tsp salt with your hands until just combined.
Shape into a loaf about 9 by 5 inches on the sheet pan. Spread the rest of the tomato sauce on top.
Bake 50 to 55 minutes, until the middle reads 160°F. Rest 10 minutes before slicing.
Meanwhile cover the potatoes with cold salted water, bring to a boil and cook 15 minutes until soft. Drain and mash with the 1/2 cup milk and salt.
Steam the green beans (or microwave per the bag) until tender.
Slice the meatloaf into 6 and pack with mash and beans.
tips: Baking it free-form on a pan (not in a loaf tin) lets the fat drain away.

recipes.name: Honey Mustard Pork, Sweet Potatoes & Green Beans
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Roast cubed sweet potatoes with 1 tablespoon oil for 15 minutes.
Stir together the honey, mustard, garlic and the rest of the oil; brush most of it over the pork.
Add the pork and green beans to the pan; roast 20 to 25 minutes, to 145°F inside.
Brush with the rest of the glaze, rest 5 minutes, slice, and divide into 6.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Peel and cube the 2 lb sweet potatoes (3/4 inch).
Mince the 3 garlic cloves. Trim the silvery skin off the pork.
steps: Toss the sweet potatoes with 1 tbsp oil and a pinch of salt. Roast 15 minutes.
Stir the 2 tbsp honey, 3 tbsp mustard, garlic and the last 1 tbsp oil together. Brush most of it over the pork and season with salt.
Push the potatoes aside. Add the pork and the frozen green beans to the pan.
Roast 20 to 25 minutes, until the pork reads 145°F.
Brush the pork with the rest of the glaze, rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Divide into 6 containers.
tips: Start checking the pork at 18 minutes; tenderloin overcooks quickly.

steps: Boil the pasta, adding the broccoli for the last 3 minutes; drain.
Cook bite-size chicken in a little oil 7 minutes; add the garlic for 1 minute.
Whisk the milk with the cornstarch, pour it in, and stir until it simmers and thickens.
Off the heat, stir in the parmesan and Greek yogurt, then toss with the pasta and broccoli.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces. Mince the 4 garlic cloves.
Whisk the 2 cups milk with the 2 tbsp cornstarch until smooth.
steps: Boil the pasta as the package says, adding the frozen broccoli for the last 3 minutes. Drain.
Heat a little oil in the skillet on medium-high. Cook the chicken about 7 minutes until browned and 165°F. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Whisk the milk mix again, pour it in and stir constantly on medium until it simmers and thickens, about 3 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the 8 tbsp parmesan and the Greek yogurt until smooth.
Toss with the pasta and broccoli. Season with salt and pepper and divide into 6.
tips: Keep stirring while the milk heats, or it can catch on the bottom.

steps: Brown the turkey with the Italian seasoning in a large deep skillet.
Add the marinara, 2 cups water and the broken dry pasta; cover and simmer 14 minutes until tender.
Stir in the spinach. Dollop the cottage cheese on top and sprinkle the mozzarella.
Cover 3 minutes to melt. Portion into 6.

prep: Break the pasta into short pieces if it's long.
steps: Brown the turkey with the Italian seasoning in the skillet on medium-high, breaking it up, about 7 minutes until no pink is left (165°F).

Cover, lower the heat and simmer 14 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the pasta is tender.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts.
Dollop the 1.5 cups cottage cheese over the top and sprinkle with the mozzarella.
Cover 3 minutes until melted. Portion into 6.
tips: Stir the bottom now and then so the pasta doesn't stick.

steps: Cook bite-size chicken in the oil 6 minutes; add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the orzo and broth; simmer uncovered 10 minutes, stirring, until the orzo is tender and creamy.
Stir in the spinach, lemon zest and juice, and the parmesan.
Season with salt and pepper and divide into 6.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces. Mince the 4 garlic cloves.
Zest one lemon, then juice both.
steps: Heat the 1 tbsp oil in the skillet on medium-high. Cook the chicken 6 minutes until browned. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the orzo and 3 cups broth. Bring to a simmer.
Simmer uncovered 10 minutes, stirring often so the orzo doesn't stick, until it's tender and creamy and the chicken reads 165°F.
Stir in the spinach, lemon zest and juice, and the parmesan.
Season with salt and pepper and divide into 6.
tips: Add a splash of water if the orzo absorbs all the broth before it's tender.

steps: Boil the pasta and keep a cup of the water.
Cook the sliced zucchini and pepper in the oil 5 minutes; add the garlic and halved tomatoes for 3 minutes.
Add the beans, pasta, parmesan, lemon juice and a splash of the pasta water.
Toss until glossy and divide into 6.

prep: Slice the 2 zucchini into half-moons and the pepper into strips. Halve the cherry tomatoes. Slice the 4 garlic cloves.

steps: Boil the pasta as the package says. Save a mug of the water, then drain.

Add the garlic and tomatoes and cook 3 minutes until the tomatoes soften.
Add the beans, pasta, 6 tbsp parmesan, lemon juice and a splash of pasta water.
Toss until glossy, season with salt and pepper, and divide into 6.
tips: Don't stir the zucchini too often; it browns better when left alone.

Mix the pasta, chicken and marinara in a baking dish; top with mozzarella and parmesan.

Mix the pasta, chicken and marinara in the baking dish.

Rest 5 minutes and cut into 6.
tips: For a browner top, broil the last 2 minutes and watch it closely.

Add the crushed tomatoes and the chicken; simmer 15 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the milk and the rest of the yogurt. Serve over rice.

Add the garlic, ginger, 2 tbsp tomato paste and the other 2 tsp curry powder and stir 1 minute.

Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the 1/2 cup milk and the rest of the yogurt.

steps: Soften the onion and peppers in the oil 8 minutes; add the garlic, cumin and paprika.
Add the crushed tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes until thick.
Make 12 wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook 6 to 8 minutes until the whites set.
Top with feta. 2 eggs and sauce per serving, with a pita.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
tools: Large deep skillet with a lid (12 inch)
prep: Chop the onion and slice the 2 peppers. Mince the 4 garlic cloves.
steps: Heat the 1 tbsp oil in the skillet on medium. Cook the onion and peppers 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, cumin and smoked paprika and stir 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes and 1/2 tsp salt. Simmer 10 minutes until thick.
Make 12 small wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook on medium-low 6 to 8 minutes, until the whites are firm. For meal prep, cook until the yolks are firm too.
Scatter the feta over. Pack 2 eggs with sauce per container, with a pita on the side.
tips: Cook in two batches of 6 eggs if your pan is smaller than 12 inches.
guide.safe: Eggs are done when the whites are firm and the yolks are thickened. Baked egg dishes are safe at 160°F in the middle.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Pierce the yolks, then microwave covered 1.5 to 2 minutes until hot.

recipes.name: Chicken Shawarma Bowls
steps: Cook the rice. Rub the chicken with the oil, cumin, paprika, half the garlic, the juice of one lemon and salt.
Roast at 425°F for 20 to 22 minutes (or pan-fry), then slice.
Stir the yogurt with the rest of the garlic and lemon for a sauce.
Pack rice, chicken, chopped cucumber, tomato and red onion, with the sauce on the side.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Start the rice.
Heat the oven to 425°F.
Mince the 4 garlic cloves. Juice both lemons separately.
Chop the cucumber and the 2 tomatoes; slice the red onion thin.
steps: Cook the 1.5 cups rice: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Bring the rice and twice its volume of water (for example 1.5 cups rice + 3 cups water) and a pinch of salt to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on 5 more minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Rub the chicken thighs with the 1 tbsp oil, cumin, smoked paprika, half the garlic, the juice of one lemon and 1 tsp salt.
Spread on the sheet pan and roast 20 to 22 minutes, until browned and 165°F. Rest 5 minutes and slice.
Stir the Greek yogurt with the rest of the garlic, the other lemon's juice and a pinch of salt.
Pack rice, chicken, cucumber, tomato and red onion in 6 containers, with the sauce on the side.
tips: For more char, broil the chicken for the last 2 minutes.
guide.safe: Chicken is safe at 165°F in the thickest part. No thermometer? Cut the thickest piece: the juices run clear and there is no pink.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Take out the vegetables and sauce, microwave the rice and chicken 2 minutes until steaming, then add them back.

recipes.name: Turkey Gyro Meatball Pitas
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Mix the turkey, oats, egg, oregano and two garlic cloves; roll 24 meatballs and bake 18 minutes.
Grate half the cucumber into the yogurt with the last garlic clove, the lemon juice and salt (tzatziki).
Chop the rest of the cucumber and the tomatoes.
Pack 4 meatballs, vegetables and tzatziki per serving with a pita.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Mince the 3 garlic cloves (2 for the meatballs, 1 for the sauce). Juice the lemon.
steps: Mix the turkey, 1/2 cup oats, egg, oregano, 2 of the garlic cloves and 1/2 tsp salt until just combined.
Roll into 24 meatballs and bake 18 minutes, until 165°F in the middle.
For tzatziki, grate half the cucumber, squeeze out the water, and stir it into the Greek yogurt with the last garlic clove, the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Chop the rest of the cucumber and the 2 tomatoes.
Pack 4 meatballs, vegetables and tzatziki per container, with a pita on the side.
tips: Squeezing the cucumber keeps the tzatziki thick.
guide.safe: Ground turkey is safe at 165°F. It should be browned all the way through with no pink left.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave only the meatballs 1 to 1.5 minutes until hot. Warm the pita 15 seconds, then add the cold vegetables and tzatziki.

recipes.name: Cuban-Style Rice, Black Beans & Eggs
steps: Cook the rice. Soften the onion and pepper in the oil 6 minutes; add the garlic, cumin and oregano.
Add the beans with half their liquid and simmer 10 minutes, mashing a few to thicken.
Boil the eggs 9 minutes (boiled eggs keep best for meal prep).
Pack rice, beans, an egg and a spoon of salsa per serving.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Start the rice.
Chop the onion and pepper, mince the 3 garlic cloves.
Open the beans; don't drain them yet.
steps: Cook the 1.5 cups rice: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Bring the rice and twice its volume of water (for example 1.5 cups rice + 3 cups water) and a pinch of salt to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on 5 more minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Heat the 1 tbsp oil in the skillet on medium. Cook the onion and pepper 6 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, cumin and oregano and stir 1 minute.
Add the beans with about half their liquid. Simmer 10 minutes, mashing a few beans to thicken. Season with salt.
Meanwhile put the 6 eggs in the small pot, cover with water by an inch, bring to a boil, then simmer 9 minutes. Move them to ice water for 5 minutes and peel.
Pack rice, beans, one egg (halved) and a spoon of salsa per container.
tips: Older eggs peel more easily than very fresh ones.
guide.safe: Eggs are done when the whites are firm and the yolks are thickened. Baked egg dishes are safe at 160°F in the middle.
guide.store: Refrigerate within 2 hours. Eat within 4 days; peeled hard-boiled eggs are best within 4 days too.
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Potato, Spinach & Cheddar Frittata
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Cook thin potato slices and the onion in the oil in an ovenproof pan, covered, 10 minutes.
Add the spinach until wilted.
Pour in the eggs beaten with salt and pepper, top with cheddar, and cook 3 minutes on the stove.
Bake 15 minutes until set. Cut into 6 wedges.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
tools: 10-inch ovenproof non-stick or cast-iron skillet with a lid
prep: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Slice the 1.5 lb potatoes very thin (about 1/8 inch). Slice the onion.
Whisk the 12 eggs with 1/2 tsp salt and pepper.
steps: Heat the 1 tbsp oil in the skillet on medium. Add the potatoes and onion with a pinch of salt, cover, and cook 10 minutes, turning now and then, until the potatoes are just tender.
Add the spinach and stir until it wilts.
Spread everything evenly, pour in the eggs and sprinkle with the cheddar.
Cook on the stove 3 minutes without stirring, until the edges start to set.
Move the pan to the oven and bake 15 minutes, until the middle is set and reads 160°F.
Use oven mitts: the handle is very hot. Rest 5 minutes, then cut into 6 wedges.
tips: Thin potato slices cook through in time; thick ones stay hard.
guide.safe: Eggs are done when the whites are firm and the yolks are thickened. Baked egg dishes are safe at 160°F in the middle.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave a wedge 60 to 90 seconds until hot. It's also good at room temperature for a short time.

recipes.name: Freezer Bean & Cheese Burritos
steps: Cook the rice. Mash the beans with the salsa and cumin over low heat until warm and thick.
Fill each tortilla with rice, beans and cheese; fold in the sides and roll tightly.
Wrap each in foil. Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months.
Reheat from frozen: unwrap, cover with a damp paper towel, and microwave 2 to 3 minutes. 2 burritos per serving.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Start the rice.
Drain and rinse the 3 cans of black beans.
Tear 10 sheets of foil.
steps: Cook the 1 cup rice: rinse, bring to a boil with 2 cups water and a pinch of salt, cover, cook on low 18 minutes, then rest 5 minutes.
Put the beans, 1 cup salsa and cumin in the saucepan on low. Mash and stir about 5 minutes until warm and thick.
Warm the tortillas 10 seconds each so they fold without cracking.
Down the middle of each, add a spoon of rice, beans and cheddar.
Fold the sides in and roll tightly from the bottom. Wrap each in foil.
Cool, then refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. 2 burritos per serving.
tips: Let the filling cool a little before rolling so the tortillas don't tear.
guide.safe: No meat or eggs to undercook: cook until the vegetables are tender and the sauce is hot all the way through.
guide.store: Refrigerate up to 4 days, or freeze up to 3 months.
guide.reheat: From frozen: unwrap, cover with a damp paper towel and microwave 2 to 3 minutes, turning halfway, until hot in the middle. From the fridge: 1 to 1.5 minutes.

recipes.name: Chicken & Cheese Quesadillas
steps: Rub the chicken with the taco seasoning and half the oil; cook 6 to 7 minutes a side until 165°F, rest and chop.
Soften the sliced pepper and onion in the rest of the oil for 5 minutes.
Layer cheese, chicken, peppers and more cheese on 4 tortillas and top with the other 4.
Toast in a dry pan 3 minutes a side until golden and melted. Cut into wedges and pack with salsa.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Slice the pepper and half the onion thin.
Rub the chicken with the 1 tbsp taco seasoning and half the oil.
steps: Heat the skillet on medium-high. Cook the chicken 6 to 7 minutes a side until it reads 165°F. Rest 5 minutes, then chop small.
Add the rest of the oil and cook the pepper and onion 5 minutes until soft. Wipe out the pan.
On 4 tortillas, layer a little cheddar, the chicken, the peppers and onion, then more cheddar. Top each with another tortilla.
Heat the dry pan on medium. Cook each quesadilla about 3 minutes a side, pressing gently, until golden and the cheese has melted.
Cut each into 4 wedges. Pack with salsa on the side.
tips: Cheese on both the top and bottom layer glues the quesadilla together.
guide.safe: Chicken is safe at 165°F in the thickest part. No thermometer? Cut the thickest piece: the juices run clear and there is no pink.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Reheat in a dry pan 2 minutes a side to keep it crisp, or microwave 60 to 90 seconds.

recipes.name: Garlic Butter Steak Bites & Potatoes
steps: Microwave the potato cubes covered 7 minutes, then brown them in the oil 8 minutes; set aside.
Sear 1-inch steak cubes in a very hot pan 2 to 3 minutes a side, in batches.
Add the butter and minced garlic for 1 minute, return the potatoes and toss.
Steam the green beans and pack with the steak and potatoes.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
tools: Large heavy skillet (cast iron is best)
prep: Cut the 2 lb potatoes into 3/4-inch cubes.
Pat the steak dry and cut into 1-inch cubes; season with 1 tsp salt and pepper.
Mince the 5 garlic cloves.
steps: Put the potatoes in the bowl with 2 tbsp water, cover and microwave 7 minutes until almost tender. Drain.
Heat the 1 tbsp oil in the skillet on medium-high. Brown the potatoes about 8 minutes, turning, until golden. Season with salt and move to a plate.
Turn the heat to high. Sear the steak in one layer, in 2 batches, 2 to 3 minutes a side, until browned and 145°F in the middle.
Turn the heat to low. Add the 3 tbsp butter and the garlic and stir 1 minute until fragrant. Return all the steak and potatoes and toss.
Steam the green beans until tender and divide everything into 5 containers.
tips: Don't crowd the pan: steak needs space to brown instead of steaming.
Garlic burns fast in hot butter; keep the heat low for that step.
guide.safe: Steak cubes are whole-muscle beef: safe at 145°F after a 3-minute rest. Cook them past that if you like them more done.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Honey Garlic Shrimp, Rice & Broccoli
steps: Cook the rice. Whisk the honey, soy sauce, cornstarch and 1/4 cup water.
Steam the broccoli florets 4 minutes.
Cook the shrimp in the butter 2 minutes a side, add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the sauce until glossy.
Pack rice, broccoli and honey garlic shrimp into 4 containers.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
tools: Steamer or saucepan with a lid
prep: Start the rice.
Thaw the shrimp in cold water 10 minutes, peel if needed and pat dry.
Cut the broccoli into florets. Mince the 4 garlic cloves.
Whisk 3 tbsp honey, 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp cornstarch and 1/4 cup water.
steps: Cook the 1.25 cups rice with 2.5 cups water: boil, cover, low 18 minutes, rest 5.
Steam the broccoli 4 minutes until bright green and just tender.
Melt the 1 tbsp butter in the skillet on medium-high. Add the shrimp in one layer and cook 2 minutes a side until pink and opaque.
Add the garlic and stir 30 seconds.
Stir the sauce, pour it in and toss about 1 minute until it thickens and coats the shrimp.
Pack rice, broccoli and shrimp with sauce into 4 containers.
tips: Take the pan off the heat as soon as the sauce is glossy; shrimp go rubbery if they keep cooking.
guide.safe: Fish is done at 145°F, or when it turns opaque and flakes easily with a fork. Shrimp are done when they turn pink and opaque and curl into a loose C shape.
guide.store: Refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.
guide.reheat: Microwave covered 1.5 to 2 minutes, just until hot.

recipes.name: Chicken Fried Rice
steps: Cook the rice ahead and chill it.
Stir-fry small pieces of chicken 5 to 6 minutes until 165°F; set aside.
Scramble the eggs, then stir-fry the vegetables and garlic 3 minutes.
Add the rice, soy sauce and sesame oil; fry 4 minutes, return the chicken and add green onions.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
tools: Saucepan with lid (cook the rice ahead)
prep: Cook the 1.5 cups rice ahead and chill it, ideally the day before.
Cut the chicken into small pieces. Beat the 3 eggs.
Mince the garlic and slice the green onions.
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in the wok on high. Stir-fry the chicken 5 to 6 minutes until 165°F. Move it to a plate.
Add a little oil, pour in the eggs and scramble until just set. Push them to the side.
Add the frozen vegetables and garlic and stir-fry 3 minutes.
Add the cold rice, breaking up clumps, with 4 tbsp soy sauce and 2 tsp sesame oil. Fry 4 minutes, tossing.
Return the chicken, add the green onions, toss 1 minute and divide into 5.
tips: Cold rice fries into separate grains; fresh rice goes sticky.
guide.safe: Chicken is safe at 165°F in the thickest part. No thermometer? Cut the thickest piece: the juices run clear and there is no pink.
guide.store: Cool fast and refrigerate within 1 hour. Eat within 3 days.
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Spaghetti with Meat Sauce
steps: Brown the beef with the chopped onion 8 minutes; add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the marinara and Italian seasoning and simmer 10 minutes.
Boil the spaghetti meanwhile.
Toss with the sauce, top with parmesan and divide into 6.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Chop the onion and mince the 3 garlic cloves.
steps: Brown the beef with the onion in the deep pan on medium-high, breaking it up, about 8 minutes until no pink is left (160°F). Spoon off extra fat.
Add the garlic and stir 1 minute.
Add the marinara and Italian seasoning. Simmer 10 minutes, stirring now and then.
Meanwhile boil the spaghetti in salted water as the package says and drain.
Toss the spaghetti with the sauce, top with the 4 tbsp parmesan and divide into 6.
tips: A splash of the pasta water helps the sauce cling to the spaghetti.
guide.safe: Ground beef and pork are safe at 160°F (no pink left). Whole cuts like steak, pork chops and tenderloin are safe at 145°F, then rest 3 minutes before slicing.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Sesame Chicken & Broccoli
steps: Cook the rice. Toss bite-size chicken with 2 tablespoons cornstarch.
Pan-fry the chicken 6 to 7 minutes until golden and 165°F.
Whisk honey, soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, garlic, the last tablespoon of cornstarch and 1/4 cup water; simmer with the chicken 2 minutes.
Steam the broccoli and pack with rice and sesame chicken; top with green onions.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Start the rice.
Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and toss with 2 tbsp of the cornstarch and a pinch of salt.
Mince the 2 garlic cloves; slice the green onions.
Whisk 3 tbsp honey, 4 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 2 tsp sesame oil, the garlic, the last 1 tbsp cornstarch and 1/4 cup water.
steps: Cook the 1.5 cups rice: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Bring the rice and twice its volume of water (for example 1.5 cups rice + 3 cups water) and a pinch of salt to a boil, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on 5 more minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in the skillet on medium-high. Fry the chicken 6 to 7 minutes, turning, until golden and 165°F.
Stir the sauce, pour it over the chicken and simmer 2 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy.
Steam the broccoli (or microwave per the bag) until tender.
Pack rice, broccoli and sesame chicken in 5 containers and top with green onions.
tips: Fry the chicken in two batches if it doesn't fit in one layer.
guide.safe: Chicken is safe at 165°F in the thickest part. No thermometer? Cut the thickest piece: the juices run clear and there is no pink.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Creamy Tuscan Chicken Pasta
steps: Boil the pasta. Cook bite-size chicken with Italian seasoning in the oil 7 minutes.
Add garlic and halved tomatoes for 2 minutes.
Stir in the milk whisked with cornstarch until it thickens, then the spinach and parmesan.
Toss with the pasta and divide into 6.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces. Mince the 4 garlic cloves. Halve the cherry tomatoes.
Whisk the 1.5 cups milk with the 1.5 tbsp cornstarch until smooth.
steps: Boil the pasta in salted water as the package says and drain.
Heat the 1 tbsp oil in the skillet on medium-high. Cook the chicken with the Italian seasoning and 1/2 tsp salt about 7 minutes until 165°F.
Add the garlic and tomatoes and cook 2 minutes.
Whisk the milk mix again, pour it in and stir until it simmers and thickens, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts, then take the pan off the heat and stir in the 6 tbsp parmesan.
Toss with the pasta and divide into 6.
tips: Keep stirring while the milk heats so it doesn't catch on the bottom.
guide.safe: Chicken is safe at 165°F in the thickest part. No thermometer? Cut the thickest piece: the juices run clear and there is no pink.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Add a splash of milk and microwave at medium power 2 to 3 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming.

recipes.name: Philly Cheesesteak Rice Bowls
steps: Cook the rice. Slice the steak very thin (easier if it's half-frozen).
Cook the sliced peppers, onion and mushrooms in the oil 7 minutes.
Push aside, sear the steak 2 to 3 minutes with the garlic powder and soy sauce, and toss together.
Top with mozzarella, cover 1 minute to melt, and pack over rice.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Start the rice.
Freeze the steak 20 minutes, then slice it as thin as you can across the grain.
Slice the 2 peppers, the onion and the mushrooms.
steps: Cook the 1.25 cups rice with 2.5 cups water: boil, cover, low 18 minutes, rest 5.
Heat the 1 tbsp oil in the skillet on medium-high. Cook the peppers, onion and mushrooms 7 minutes until soft and browned.
Push the vegetables to the side. Add the steak, garlic powder, 1 tbsp soy sauce and a pinch of pepper. Sear 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until no longer pink.
Toss everything together, scatter the mozzarella on top, cover 1 minute until melted.
Pack over rice in 5 containers.
tips: Thin slices are the secret: they cook in 2 minutes and stay tender.
guide.safe: Thin steak slices are safe once browned with no pink left; whole-muscle beef is safe at 145°F.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Vegetable Lo Mein with Egg
steps: Boil the spaghetti, drain and toss with 1 teaspoon sesame oil.
Scramble the eggs and set aside.
Stir-fry the mushrooms, cabbage, carrots, pepper and garlic 4 minutes.
Add noodles, soy sauce, hoisin, the rest of the sesame oil and the eggs; toss 2 minutes and add green onions.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Shred the cabbage, cut the 2 carrots into matchsticks, slice the pepper and mushrooms.
Mince the 3 garlic cloves, slice the green onions. Beat the 4 eggs.
steps: Boil the spaghetti until just tender. Drain and toss with 1 tsp of the sesame oil.
Heat a little oil in the wok on medium. Scramble the eggs until just set and move them to a plate.
Turn the heat to high. Stir-fry the mushrooms 2 minutes, then add the cabbage, carrots, pepper and garlic for 3 to 4 minutes, until crisp-tender.
Add the noodles, 5 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp hoisin and the last 1 tsp sesame oil. Toss 2 minutes until coated.
Fold the eggs back in with the green onions and divide into 5.
tips: Use tongs to toss the noodles so the sauce coats them evenly.
guide.safe: Eggs are done when the whites are firm and the yolks are thickened. Baked egg dishes are safe at 160°F in the middle.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Crispy Black Bean Tacos
steps: Mash the drained beans with the cumin, chili powder and a pinch of salt.
Fill warmed tortillas with beans and cheese, fold, and crisp in a lightly oiled pan 2 to 3 minutes a side.
Toss the shredded cabbage with yogurt, the juice of one lime and salt.
Pack 3 tacos each with slaw, salsa, sliced avocado and lime on the side.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Drain and rinse the 2 cans of black beans.
Shred the cabbage. Juice one lime and cut the other into wedges.
steps: Mash the beans with the cumin, chili powder and 1/2 tsp salt until mostly smooth.
Warm the tortillas 20 seconds in the microwave under a damp paper towel so they bend without cracking.
Spread beans on half of each tortilla, add a little cheddar and fold over.
Brush the skillet with the 1 tbsp oil and heat on medium. Cook the tacos 2 to 3 minutes a side until crisp and the cheese has melted.
Toss the cabbage with the Greek yogurt, lime juice and a pinch of salt for slaw.
Pack 3 tacos each with slaw, salsa, avocado and a lime wedge on the side.
tips: Slice the avocado on the day you eat it so it stays green.
guide.safe: No meat or eggs to undercook: cook until the vegetables are tender and the sauce is hot all the way through.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Reheat the tacos in a dry pan 2 minutes a side (crispest) or microwave 45 to 60 seconds. Add the cold slaw after.

recipes.name: Garlic Tomato Pasta with Mozzarella
steps: Boil the pasta; keep a cup of the water.
Cook the sliced garlic in the oil 1 minute, add the tomatoes and cook 6 minutes until they burst.
Add the beans, spinach, Italian seasoning, pasta, parmesan and a splash of pasta water.
Off the heat, stir in the mozzarella so it goes melty, and divide into 6.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Slice the 5 garlic cloves thin.
Drain and rinse the white beans.
steps: Boil the pasta in salted water as the package says. Save a mug of the water, then drain.
Heat the 3 tbsp olive oil in the skillet on medium. Cook the garlic 1 minute until fragrant, not brown.
Add the 2 pints of cherry tomatoes and a pinch of salt. Cook about 6 minutes, stirring, until they burst and turn saucy (press them with a spoon).
Add the beans, spinach and Italian seasoning and stir until the spinach wilts.
Add the pasta, the 4 tbsp parmesan and a splash of pasta water and toss.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the mozzarella so it goes melty. Divide into 6.
tips: Tear the mozzarella into small pieces so it melts evenly.
guide.safe: No meat or eggs to undercook: cook until the tomatoes burst and everything is hot.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Bang Bang Shrimp Bowls
steps: Cook the rice. Stir the yogurt, sriracha and honey for the sauce.
Toss the shrimp in cornstarch and a pinch of salt; pan-fry in the oil 2 minutes a side until pink and crisp.
Slice the cucumber and grate the carrots.
Pack rice, shrimp and vegetables with the sauce on the side; top with green onions.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Start the rice.
Thaw the shrimp in cold water 10 minutes, peel if needed and pat very dry.
Slice the cucumber, grate the 2 carrots, slice the green onions.
Stir the Greek yogurt with the 3 tsp sriracha and 2 tbsp honey for the sauce.
steps: Cook the 1.25 cups rice with 2.5 cups water: boil, cover, low 18 minutes, rest 5.
Toss the shrimp with the 2 tbsp cornstarch and 1/2 tsp salt.
Heat the 1 tbsp oil in the skillet on medium-high. Cook the shrimp in one layer 2 minutes a side until pink, opaque and lightly crisp.
Pack rice, shrimp, cucumber and carrots in 4 containers.
Put the sauce in small cups on the side and top with green onions.
tips: Real bang bang sauce uses mayo; Greek yogurt keeps the creamy kick with more protein.
guide.safe: Fish is done at 145°F, or when it turns opaque and flakes easily with a fork. Shrimp are done when they turn pink and opaque and curl into a loose C shape.
guide.store: Refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.
guide.reheat: Take out the vegetables and sauce. Microwave the rice and shrimp covered 1 to 1.5 minutes, just until hot, then add them back.

recipes.name: Egg & Cheese Breakfast Quesadillas
steps: Soften the diced pepper and onion in the oil 4 minutes, then wilt in the spinach.
Add the beaten eggs and scramble over medium-low until just set.
Spread egg and cheddar over half of each tortilla and fold.
Toast in a dry pan 2 to 3 minutes a side until golden and melted. Pack 2 each with salsa.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Dice the bell pepper and half the onion small.
Beat the 8 eggs with 1/4 tsp salt and some pepper.
Roughly chop the 2 oz spinach.
steps: Heat the 1 tbsp oil in the skillet on medium. Cook the pepper and onion 4 minutes until soft, then stir in the spinach until it wilts.
Turn the heat to medium-low, pour in the eggs and stir slowly with the spatula 2 to 3 minutes until just set but still soft. Move to a plate and wipe out the pan.
Lay out the 8 tortillas. Put some cheddar, a share of the eggs, then a little more cheddar on one half of each and fold it over.
Heat the dry pan on medium. Cook 2 or 3 quesadillas at a time, 2 to 3 minutes a side, until golden and the cheese has melted.
Let them cool, then pack 2 per container with the salsa in a small cup on the side.
tips: Take the eggs off while they still look a little wet; they finish cooking in the quesadilla.
guide.safe: Eggs are done when the whites are firm and the yolks are thickened. Baked egg dishes are safe at 160°F in the middle.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Reheat in a dry pan 2 minutes a side to keep them crisp, or microwave 60 to 90 seconds until hot in the middle.

recipes.name: One-Pot Cheeseburger Pasta
steps: Brown the beef with the chopped onion 8 minutes until no pink is left; drain the fat.
Stir in the tomato paste, mustard, garlic powder and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the broth, milk and pasta; simmer covered, stirring often, 10 to 12 minutes until the pasta is tender.
Off the heat, stir in the cheddar until melted and divide into 6.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
tools: Large deep skillet or pot with a lid
prep: Chop the onion.
Measure the 3 cups broth and 1.5 cups milk.
Have the 12 oz pasta (small shells or elbows work best) ready.
steps: Heat the pan on medium-high. Brown the 1.25 lb beef with the onion about 8 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink is left (160°F). Spoon off the fat.
Stir in the 2 tbsp tomato paste, 1 tbsp mustard, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp paprika and 1 tsp salt for 1 minute.
Pour in the broth and milk, stir in the pasta and bring to a gentle boil.
Cover, turn the heat to medium-low and simmer 10 to 12 minutes, stirring every few minutes so it doesn't stick, until the pasta is tender and most of the liquid is gone.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the 6 oz cheddar until melted and creamy. Divide into 6.
tips: Keep it at a gentle simmer: milk can catch on the bottom if the heat is too high.
It thickens as it cools; add a splash of milk when you reheat.
guide.safe: Ground beef and pork are safe at 160°F (no pink left). Whole cuts like steak, pork chops and tenderloin are safe at 145°F, then rest 3 minutes before slicing.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
guide.reheat: Microwave covered, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through (165°F), about 2 to 3 minutes per container. Thaw frozen portions overnight in the fridge first.

recipes.name: Lemon Feta Chickpea Orzo
steps: Boil the orzo in salted water about 9 minutes; drain.
Cook the garlic in the oil 1 minute, add the chickpeas, halved tomatoes and oregano and cook 4 minutes.
Stir in the spinach until wilted, then the orzo, lemon zest and juice.
Fold in the feta and divide into 5.

guide.pantry: You'll also need salt, black pepper, water and a little cooking oil or spray.
prep: Drain and rinse the 2 cans of chickpeas.
Halve the cherry tomatoes and mince the 4 garlic cloves.
Zest the lemon, then juice it.
steps: Boil the 12 oz orzo in salted water about 9 minutes until tender. Drain.
Heat the 3 tbsp olive oil in the skillet on medium. Cook the garlic 1 minute, then add the chickpeas, tomatoes and 1 tsp oregano and cook 4 minutes.
Add the 5 oz spinach and stir until it wilts.
Stir in the orzo, the lemon zest and juice and 1/2 tsp salt.
Fold in the 4 oz feta and divide into 5 containers.
tips: It tastes good cold too, like a pasta salad.
guide.safe: No meat or eggs to undercook: cook until the spinach wilts and everything is hot.
guide.store: Cool it within 2 hours of cooking, then seal in containers in the fridge. Eat within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (best quality).
